title.zh: 卷八十二 列傳第七 十一宗諸子
title.en: Volume 82 Biographies 7: Sons of the Eleven Zongs
title.raw: 卷八十二 列傳第七 十一宗諸子 Volume 82 Biographies 7: Sons of the Eleven Zongs

sentences.zh: 十一宗諸子

translations.literal: Sons of the Eleven Zongs.
translations.idiomatic: Sons of the Eleven Zongs.

sentences.zh: 玄宗三十子：劉華妃生琮、第六子琬、第十二子璲，趙麗妃生瑛，元獻皇后生肅宗皇帝，錢妃生琰，皇甫德儀生瑤，劉才人生琚，武惠妃生一、第十五子敏、第十八子瑁、第二十一子琦，高婕妤生璬，郭順儀生璘，柳婕妤生玢，鐘美人生環，盧美人生瑝，閻才人生玼，王美人生珪，陳才人生珙，鄭才人生瑱，武賢儀生璿、第三十子璥；

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong had thirty sons: Consort Liu of Huahua bore Cong, the sixth son Wan, and the twelfth son Xun; Consort Zhao Li bore Ying; Empress Yuanxian bore Emperor Suzong; Consort Qian bore Yan; Lady Huangfu bore Yao; Lady Liu bore Ju; Consort Wu Hui bore Yi, the fifteenth son Min, the eighteenth son Mao, and the twenty-first son Qi; Lady Gao bore Wei; Lady Guo Shun bore Lin; Lady Liu of Willow bore Bin; Lady Zhong bore Huan; Lady Lu bore Huang; Lady Yan bore Ci; Lady Wang bore Gui; Lady Chen bore Gong; Lady Zheng bore Tian; Lady Wu Xian bore Xuan and the thirtieth son Jing;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong had thirty sons. Consort Liu of Huahua bore Cong, the sixth son Wan, and the twelfth son Xun. Consort Zhao Li bore Ying; Empress Yuanxian bore Emperor Suzong; Consort Qian bore Yan. Lady Huangfu bore Yao; Lady Liu bore Ju. Consort Wu Hui bore Yi, the fifteenth son Min, the eighteenth son Mao, and the twenty-first son Qi. Lady Gao bore Wei; Lady Guo Shun bore Lin; Lady Liu of Willow bore Bin; Lady Zhong bore Huan; Lady Lu bore Huang; Lady Yan bore Ci; Lady Wang bore Gui; Lady Chen bore Gong; Lady Zheng bore Tian. Lady Wu Xian bore Xuan and the thirtieth son Jing.

sentences.zh: 余七子夭，母氏失傳。

translations.literal: Seven other sons died young; their mothers' names are not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Seven other sons died in infancy, and the names of their mothers have not been preserved.

sentences.zh: 奉天皇帝琮，景雲元年，王許昌郡，與真定王同封。

translations.literal: Fengtian Emperor Cong—in the first year of Jingyun was made Prince of Xuchang commandery, enfeoffed together with the Prince of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Cong, later posthumously honored as Emperor Fengtian, was first enfeoffed as Prince of Xuchang in Jingyun 1, on the same occasion as the Prince of Zhending.

sentences.zh: 先天元年，進王郯，與郢王同封。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiantian, he was advanced to Prince of Tan, enfeoffed together with the Prince of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiantian 1 he was promoted to Prince of Tan and enfeoffed together with the Prince of Ying.

sentences.zh: 開元四年，領安西大都護、安撫河東關內隴右諸蕃大使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaiyuan, he held the posts of Protector-General of Anxi and Commissioner for Pacifying the Eastern Barbarians of Hedong, Guannei, Longxi, and the various tribes.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 4 he was appointed Protector-General of Anxi and commissioner charged with pacifying the tribes of Hedong, Guannei, and Longxi.

sentences.zh: 十三年，徙王慶，與忠、棣、榮、光、儀、潁、永、壽、延、盛、濟十一王同封。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, he was transferred to Prince of Qing, enfeoffed together with the eleven princes of Zhong, Di, Rong, Guang, Yi, Ying, Yong, Shou, Yan, Sheng, and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13 he was transferred to Prince of Qing, enfeoffed on the same day as the eleven princes of Zhong, Di, Rong, Guang, Yi, Ying, Yong, Shou, Yan, Sheng, and Ji.

sentences.zh: 十五年，與十王並領節度，不出閤。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, together with ten princes he simultaneously received military commissions as circuit commissioners, but did not leave the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In year 15 he and ten other princes were all given frontier military commissions as circuit commissioners, yet none of them left the palace to take up their posts.

sentences.zh: 琮以涼州都督兼河西諸軍節度大使。

translations.literal: Cong served as Military Governor of Liangzhou and concurrently as Grand Military Commissioner of the Hexi armies.
translations.idiomatic: Cong held Liangzhou as military governor and concurrently commanded the Hexi armies.

sentences.zh: 天寶元年，改節河東。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianbao, his commission was changed to Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 1 his command was transferred to Hedong.

sentences.zh: 十載薨，贈太子，謚靖德。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he died; he was posthumously honored as crown prince, with the posthumous title Jingde.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year 10 and was posthumously honored as crown prince with the title Prince Jingde.

sentences.zh: 肅宗立，詔曰：「靖德太子琮，親則朕兄，睿悊聰明，朕昔踐儲極，顧誠非次，君父有命，不敢違，永言懇讓，不克如素。

translations.literal: When Suzong ascended the throne, an edict read: 'Crown Prince Jingde Cong is my elder brother by blood. Wise, discerning, and intelligent—in days past when I took the throne, I knew the succession was not rightfully mine. My father and sovereign had commanded it, and I dared not disobey. I have ever spoken of yielding in earnest, yet could not restore matters as they once were.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Suzong took the throne, he issued an edict: 'Crown Prince Jingde Cong was my elder brother by blood—wise, discerning, and clear-minded. When I first ascended the throne, I knew the succession was not rightfully mine, yet our father and sovereign had commanded it and I dared not disobey. I have ever wished in earnest to yield the throne, yet could not restore things as they once were.

sentences.zh: 宜進謚奉天皇帝，妃竇為恭應皇后。

translations.literal: His posthumous title should be advanced to Fengtian Emperor, and his consort Dou should be honored as Empress Gongying.'
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title should be raised to Emperor Fengtian, and his consort, Lady Dou, should be honored as Empress Gongying.'

sentences.zh: 」詔尚書右仆射裴冕持節改葬，群臣素服臨送達禮門，帝禦門哭以過喪，墓號齊陵。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Right Vice Director of the Secretariat Pei Mian to proceed with credentials and reinter the body. The ministers attended in plain dress and escorted the coffin to the Gate of Rites; the emperor came to the gate and wept in mourning beyond what custom required. The tomb was named Qiling.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Pei Mian, Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, to proceed with imperial credentials and oversee the reinterment. Ministers in plain mourning dress escorted the coffin to the Gate of Rites, and the emperor came to the gate and wept beyond the prescribed rites. The tomb was named Qiling.

sentences.zh: 無子，以太子瑛子俅嗣王。

translations.literal: He had no sons; Ying's son Qiu was made to succeed to the princedom.
translations.idiomatic: He left no sons, so Qiu, son of Crown Prince Ying, was appointed to succeed to the title.

sentences.zh: 琮始名嗣直，太子嗣謙，棣王嗣真，鄂王嗣初，靖恭太子嗣玄。

translations.literal: Cong was originally named Sizhi; the crown prince was named Siqian; the Prince of Di was named Sizhen; the Prince of E was named Sichu; Crown Prince Jinggong was named Sixuan.
translations.idiomatic: Cong had originally been named Sizhi; the crown prince Siqian; the Prince of Di Sizhen; the Prince of E Sichu; and Crown Prince Jinggong Sixuan.

sentences.zh: 開元十三年，更名曰潭，曰鴻，曰洽，曰涓，曰滉。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kaiyuan, their names were changed to Tan, Hong, Qia, Juan, and Huang.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 13 their names were changed to Tan, Hong, Qia, Juan, and Huang.

sentences.zh: 後十年改今名。

translations.literal: Ten years later they were given their present names.
translations.idiomatic: A decade later they received the names by which they are now known.

sentences.zh: 太子瑛，始王真定，進王郢。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Ying was first enfeoffed as Prince of Zhending, then advanced to Prince of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Ying was first created Prince of Zhending, then promoted to Prince of Ying.

sentences.zh: 開元三年，立為皇太子。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaiyuan, he was established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 3 he was formally invested as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 七年，詔太子、諸王入國學行齒胄禮，太常擇日謁孔子，太子獻。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, an edict ordered the crown prince and the princes to enter the Directorate of Education and perform the ceremony of donning armor; the Court of Imperial Sacrifices chose a day to visit Confucius, and the crown prince made the offerings.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 an edict ordered the crown prince and the princes to enter the imperial academy and perform the coming-of-age ceremony in armor. The Court of Imperial Sacrifices chose a day for the visit to Confucius, and the crown prince led the offerings.

sentences.zh: 詔右散騎常侍褚無量執經，群臣、學官、諸生以差賜帛。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Right Regular Attendant Chu Wuliang to expound the classics; ministers, academy officials, and students received gifts of silk according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Chu Wuliang, Right Regular Attendant, to expound the classics, and ministers, academy officials, and students received gifts of silk according to rank.

sentences.zh: 明年，瑛加元服，見太廟。

translations.literal: The following year, Ying received the capping ceremony and visited the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Ying underwent the capping ceremony and paid homage at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 十六年，詔九品官息女可配太子者，有司采閱待進止，以太常少卿薛縚女為妃。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, an edict declared that daughters of officials of the ninth rank and above who were suitable to marry the crown prince might be selected; the relevant offices were to review candidates and await the throne's decision. Xue Zong's daughter was made consort.
translations.idiomatic: In year 16 an edict declared that daughters of officials down to the ninth rank, if deemed suitable for the crown prince, were to be reviewed by the relevant offices and presented for the throne's decision. The daughter of Vice Minister of Rites Xue Zong was chosen as consort.

sentences.zh: 帝種麥苑中，瑛、諸王侍登，帝曰：「是將薦宗廟，故親之，亦欲若等知稼穡之難。

translations.literal: The emperor planted wheat in the palace park. Ying and the princes attended him as he climbed the rise. The emperor said: 'This is to be offered in the ancestral temple, so I tend it myself. I also wish you to know how hard the work of sowing and reaping is.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor planted wheat in the palace park, and Ying and the princes attended him on the rise. The emperor said, 'This grain is destined for the ancestral temple, so I tend it myself—and I want you to understand how arduous the work of sowing and harvest truly is.'

sentences.zh: 」因分賜侍臣，曰：「《春秋》書『無麥禾』，古所甚重。

translations.literal: He then distributed shares to the attending ministers and said: 'The Spring and Autumn Annals records "no wheat, no grain"—the ancients regarded this as a matter of grave importance.'
translations.idiomatic: He then divided shares among the attending ministers and said, 'The Spring and Autumn Annals records "no wheat, no grain"—the ancients treated such failure as a matter of the gravest import.'

sentences.zh: 比詔使者閱田畝，所對不以實，故朕自蒔以觀其成」雲。

translations.literal: Recently I ordered envoys to inspect the fields, but their reports did not reflect the truth. That is why I have planted the crop myself to observe how it grows,' he said.
translations.idiomatic: Lately I ordered envoys to inspect the fields, yet their reports did not reflect the truth. That is why I have planted this crop myself, to see how it truly grows,' he said.

sentences.zh: 初，瑛母以倡進，善歌舞，帝在潞得幸。

translations.literal: At the outset, Ying's mother had entered the palace as a singing-girl, skilled in song and dance. While the emperor was at Lu, she won his favor.
translations.idiomatic: In the beginning Ying's mother had been brought into the palace as a singing-girl, skilled in song and dance. While the emperor was still at Lu she won his favor.

sentences.zh: 及即位，擢妃父元禮、兄常奴皆至大官。

translations.literal: When he ascended the throne, he promoted her father Yuanli and her elder brother Changnu to high office.
translations.idiomatic: Once he took the throne, he promoted her father Yuanli and her elder brother Changnu to high office.

sentences.zh: 鄂、光二王母亦帝為臨淄王時以色選。

translations.literal: The mothers of the Princes of E and Guang had likewise been chosen for their beauty when the emperor was Prince of Linzi.
translations.idiomatic: The mothers of the Princes of E and Guang had likewise been chosen for their beauty when the emperor was still Prince of Linzi.

sentences.zh: 及武惠妃寵幸傾後宮，生壽王，愛與諸子絕等。

translations.literal: When Consort Wu Hui's favor eclipsed the entire inner palace and she bore the Prince of Shou, the emperor's love for him surpassed all his other sons by far.
translations.idiomatic: When Consort Wu Hui's favor came to eclipse the entire inner palace and she bore the Prince of Shou, the emperor's love for that son surpassed all his other sons by far.

sentences.zh: 而太子、二王以母失職，頗怏怏。

translations.literal: The crown prince and the two princes, their mothers having lost standing, were deeply discontented.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince and the two princes, whose mothers had fallen from favor, grew deeply resentful.

sentences.zh: 惠妃女咸宜公主婿楊洄揣妃旨，伺太子短，嘩為醜語，惠妃訴於帝，且泣，帝大怒，召宰相議廢之。

translations.literal: Consort Wu Hui's daughter, Princess Xianyi, had married Yang Hui. Reading the consort's intent, he watched for the crown prince's faults and spread ugly rumors. Consort Wu Hui complained to the emperor and wept. The emperor was furious and summoned the chief ministers to discuss deposing him.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Wu Hui's daughter, Princess Xianyi, had married Yang Hui. Divining the consort's wishes, he watched for the crown prince's faults and spread ugly rumors about him. Consort Wu Hui complained to the emperor and wept. The emperor flew into a rage and summoned the chief ministers to discuss deposing the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 中書令張九齡諫曰：「太子、諸王日受聖訓，天下共慶。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Zhang Jiuling remonstrated: 'The crown prince and the princes daily receive the sage's instruction—the realm rejoices with them.'
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Zhang Jiuling remonstrated: 'The crown prince and the princes receive Your Majesty's instruction every day, and the realm rejoices in them.'

sentences.zh: 陛下享國久，子孫蕃衍，奈何一日棄三子。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has long enjoyed the throne and your descendants multiply—how can you in a single day cast aside three sons?'
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has long held the throne and your descendants multiply—how can you cast aside three sons in a single day?'

sentences.zh: 昔晉獻公惑嬖姬之讒，申生憂死，國乃大亂；

translations.literal: In former times Duke Xian of Jin was beguiled by a favorite woman's slander; Shen Sheng died in grief and the state fell into great disorder;
translations.idiomatic: In former times Duke Xian of Jin was beguiled by a favorite woman's slander; Shen Sheng died in grief and the state fell into chaos;

sentences.zh: 漢武帝信江充巫蠱，禍及太子，京師蹀血；

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han believed Jiang Chong's witchcraft charges, and disaster reached the crown prince until the capital ran with blood;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Han believed Jiang Chong's witchcraft charges, and disaster reached the crown prince until the capital ran with blood;

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝有賢子，賈後譖之，乃至喪亡；

translations.literal: Emperor Hui of Jin had a worthy son, yet Empress Jia slandered him and the dynasty was lost;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hui of Jin had a worthy son, yet Empress Jia slandered him and the dynasty was lost;

sentences.zh: 隋文帝聽後言，廢太子勇，遂失天下。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui listened to his empress's words, deposed Crown Prince Yong, and thereafter lost the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Sui listened to his empress, deposed Crown Prince Yong, and thereafter lost the realm.

sentences.zh: 今太子無過，二王賢。

translations.literal: Now the crown prince is without fault, and the two princes are worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Today the crown prince is without fault, and the two princes are worthy men.

sentences.zh: 父子之道，天性也，雖有失，尚當掩之。

translations.literal: The way of father and son is rooted in nature; even when there are faults, they should still be covered over.
translations.idiomatic: The bond between father and son is rooted in nature; even when faults exist, they ought still to be covered over.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下裁赦。

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty to judge and pardon them.'
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to judge wisely and show mercy.'

sentences.zh: 」帝默然，太子得不廢。

translations.literal: The emperor fell silent, and the crown prince was not deposed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fell silent, and the crown prince was spared.

sentences.zh: 俄而九齡罷，李林甫專國，數稱壽王美以揠妃意，妃果德之。

translations.literal: Before long Jiuling was dismissed; Li Linfu monopolized the government and repeatedly praised the Prince of Shou's virtues to please the consort, and she indeed felt grateful to him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Jiuling was dismissed. Li Linfu monopolized the government and repeatedly praised the Prince of Shou's virtues to please the consort, and she came to regard him with gratitude.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，洄復構瑛、瑤、琚與妃之兄薛銹異謀。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, Hui again fabricated a plot involving Ying, Yao, Ju, and the consort's elder brother Xue Xiu in a conspiracy of divergent designs.
translations.idiomatic: In year 25 Hui again fabricated a plot implicating Ying, Yao, and Ju together with the consort's elder brother Xue Xiu in a treasonous conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 惠妃使人詭召太子、二王，曰：「宮中有賊，請介以入。

translations.literal: Consort Wu Hui sent someone to summon the crown prince and the two princes under false pretenses, saying: 'There are bandits in the palace—please come in wearing armor.'
translations.idiomatic: Consort Wu Hui sent someone to summon the crown prince and the two princes under false pretenses, saying, 'There are bandits in the palace—please come in wearing armor.'

sentences.zh: 」太子從之。

translations.literal: The crown prince complied.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince complied.

sentences.zh: 妃白帝曰：「太子、二王謀反，甲而來。

translations.literal: The consort reported to the emperor: 'The crown prince and the two princes are plotting rebellion—they have come in armor.'
translations.idiomatic: The consort reported to the emperor, 'The crown prince and the two princes are plotting rebellion—they have come in armor.'

sentences.zh: 」帝使中人視之，如言，遽召宰相林甫議，答曰：「陛下家事，非臣所宜豫。

translations.literal: The emperor sent eunuchs to verify it; finding the report true, he hastily summoned Chief Minister Linfu to discuss the matter. Linfu replied: 'This is Your Majesty's family affair—not something your servant should venture upon.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent eunuchs to verify the report; finding it true, he hastily summoned Chief Minister Linfu. Linfu replied, 'This is Your Majesty's family affair—not something a subject should venture upon.'

sentences.zh: 」帝意決，乃詔：「太子瑛、鄂王瑤、光王琚同惡均罪，並廢為庶人；

translations.literal: The emperor's mind was made up, and an edict declared: 'Crown Prince Ying, the Prince of E Yao, and the Prince of Guang Ju share equal guilt in the same evil deed—all three are deposed to commoner status;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's mind was made up. An edict declared, 'Crown Prince Ying, the Prince of E Yao, and the Prince of Guang Ju share equal guilt in the same evil deed—all three are deposed to commoner status;

sentences.zh: 銹賜死。

translations.literal: Xiu is granted death.'
translations.idiomatic: Xiu is sentenced to death.'

sentences.zh: 」瑛、瑤、琚尋遇害，天下冤之，號「三庶人」。

translations.literal: Ying, Yao, and Ju were soon killed. The realm regarded it as a grievous injustice and called them 'the Three Commoners.'
translations.idiomatic: Ying, Yao, and Ju were soon killed. The realm regarded their deaths as a grievous injustice and called them 'the Three Commoners.'

sentences.zh: 歲中，惠妃數見庶人為祟，因大病。

translations.literal: Within the year Consort Wu Hui repeatedly saw the commoners haunting her and fell gravely ill.
translations.idiomatic: Within the year Consort Wu Hui repeatedly saw the deposed princes haunting her and fell gravely ill.

sentences.zh: 夜召巫祈之，請改葬，且射行刑者瘞之，訖不解。

translations.literal: At night she summoned shamans to pray, requested reburial, and had those who carried out the executions shot and buried—yet she was not cured.
translations.idiomatic: At night she summoned shamans to pray, requested that the victims be reburied, and had the executioners shot and buried as well—yet she was not cured.

sentences.zh: 妃死，崇亡。

translations.literal: When the consort died, the hauntings ceased.
translations.idiomatic: When the consort died, the hauntings ceased.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年，詔贈瑛皇太子，瑤等復王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoying, an edict posthumously restored Ying as crown prince and restored Yao and the others to princely rank.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoying 1 an edict posthumously restored Ying as crown prince and returned Yao and the others to princely rank.

sentences.zh: 瑛子五人：儼、伸、倩、俅、備。

translations.literal: Ying had five sons: Yan, Shen, Qian, Qiu, and Bei.
translations.idiomatic: Ying had five sons: Yan, Shen, Qian, Qiu, and Bei.

sentences.zh: 瑛之廢，帝使慶王畜儼等為子。

translations.literal: When Ying was deposed, the emperor had the Prince of Qing raise Yan and the others as his own sons.
translations.idiomatic: When Ying was deposed, the emperor had the Prince of Qing take Yan and the others and raise them as his own sons.

sentences.zh: 儼封新平郡王，伸平原郡王，俅嗣慶王，備太仆卿，倩失傳。

translations.literal: Yan was enfeoffed as Prince of Xinping commandery; Shen as Prince of Pingyuan commandery; Qiu succeeded to the Prince of Qing; Bei became Minister of the Imperial Stud; Qian's record is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was enfeoffed as Prince of Xinping; Shen as Prince of Pingyuan; Qiu succeeded to the title of Prince of Qing; Bei became Minister of the Imperial Stud; Qian's record is lost.

sentences.zh: 隸王琰，開元二年始王鄫，與鄂、鄄二王同封。

translations.literal: Prince Yan was first enfeoffed as Prince of Zeng in the second year of Kaiyuan, together with the Princes of E and Juancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yan was first enfeoffed as Prince of Zeng in Kaiyuan 2, together with the Princes of E and Juancheng.

sentences.zh: 後徙王棣，領太原牧、太原以北諸軍節度大使。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Prince of Di, holding the post of Governor of Taiyuan and Grand Military Commissioner of all armies north of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to Prince of Di, serving as Governor of Taiyuan and Grand Military Commissioner of all armies north of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，為武威郡都督，經略節度河西、隴右。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he served as Military Governor of Wuwei commandery and commissioner overseeing Hexi and Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Tianbao era he served as military governor of Wuwei and commissioner overseeing Hexi and Longyou.

sentences.zh: 會妃韋以過置別室，而二孺人爭寵不平，求巫者密置符琰履中以求媚。

translations.literal: Once his consort Lady Wei was confined to a separate chamber for an offense, two young concubines quarreled over favor and, seeking a sorcerer's help, secretly placed talismans in Yan's shoes to win his affection.
translations.idiomatic: Once his consort Lady Wei was confined to a separate chamber for an offense. Two young concubines quarreled over favor and, seeking a sorcerer's aid, secretly placed talismans in Yan's shoes to win his affection.

sentences.zh: 仇人告琰厭魅上，帝伺其朝，使人取履視之，信。

translations.literal: An enemy reported that Yan had used sorcery against the emperor. The emperor waited until Yan came to court, then sent men to fetch his shoes and inspect them; finding the report credible,
translations.idiomatic: An enemy reported that Yan had used sorcery against the emperor. The emperor waited until Yan came to court, then sent men to fetch his shoes and inspect them—and found the report credible.

sentences.zh: 帝怒責琰，琰頓首謝曰：「臣罪宜死，然臣與婦不相見二年，有二孺人爭長，臣恐此三人為之。

translations.literal: the emperor angrily rebuked Yan. Yan kowtowed and said: 'Your servant deserves death. Yet I have not seen my wife for two years, and two concubines contend for precedence—I fear these three women are responsible.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor angrily rebuked Yan. Yan kowtowed and said, 'Your servant deserves death. Yet I have not seen my wife for two years, and two concubines contend for precedence—I fear these three women are responsible.'

sentences.zh: 」及推，果驗。

translations.literal: When the matter was investigated, it proved true.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter was investigated, it proved true.

sentences.zh: 然帝猶疑琰，怒未置，太子以下皆為請，乃囚於鷹狗坊，以憂薨，妃，縚之女，無子，還本宗。

translations.literal: Yet the emperor still harbored doubts about Yan and his anger was not assuaged. The crown prince and all below him pleaded on Yan's behalf, whereupon Yan was imprisoned in the Hawk and Hound Yard and died of grief. His consort, Zong's daughter, had no sons and was returned to her clan.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the emperor still harbored doubts about Yan, and his anger was not assuaged. The crown prince and all the princes below him pleaded on Yan's behalf, whereupon Yan was imprisoned in the Hawk and Hound Yard and died of grief. His consort, Zong's daughter, had no sons and was returned to her clan.

sentences.zh: 琰凡五十五子，得王者四人，僎王汝南郡，僑宜都，俊濟南，侒順化；

translations.literal: Yan had fifty-five sons in all; four received princely rank: Fu as Prince of Runan commandery, Qiao of Yidu, Jun of Jinan, and An of Shunhua;
translations.idiomatic: Yan had fifty-five sons in all; four received princely rank: Fu as Prince of Runan, Qiao of Yidu, Jun of Jinan, and An of Shunhua;

sentences.zh: 僚太仆卿，俠國子祭酒，仁殿中監，僾秘書監。

translations.literal: Liao became Minister of the Imperial Stud; Xia became Chancellor of the Directorate of Education; Ren became Director of the Palace Administration; Ai became Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Liao became Minister of the Imperial Stud; Xia became Chancellor of the Directorate of Education; Ren became Director of the Palace Administration; and Ai became Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年，詔復琰王爵。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoying, an edict restored Yan's princely title.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoying 1 an edict restored Yan's princely title.

sentences.zh: 鄂王瑤，既封，遙領幽州都督、河北節度大使。

translations.literal: The Prince of E, Yao—once enfeoffed—held the posts of Military Governor of Youzhou and Grand Military Commissioner of Hebei in absentia.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of E, Yao—once enfeoffed—held the posts of military governor of Youzhou and grand military commissioner of Hebei in absentia.

sentences.zh: 開元二十三年，與榮、光、儀、潁、永、壽、延、盛、濟、信、義十一王並授開府儀同三司，實封二千戶。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Kaiyuan, together with the eleven princes of Rong, Guang, Ceremonial Rites, Ying, Yong, Shou, Yan, Sheng, Ji, Xin, and Righteousness, he was all granted the honorary rank of Grand Master with Gold Seal and Purple Cord, with an actual fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 23 he and the eleven princes of Rong, Guang, Ceremonial Rites, Ying, Yong, Shou, Yan, Sheng, Ji, Xin, and Righteousness were all granted the honorary rank of Grand Master with Gold Seal and Purple Cord, with an actual fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 詔詣東宮、尚書省，上日百官集送，有司供張設樂。

translations.literal: An edict ordered them to proceed to the Eastern Palace and the Secretariat; on the appointed day the hundred officials assembled to escort them, and the relevant offices provided banners and music.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered them to proceed to the Eastern Palace and the Secretariat. On the appointed day the hundred officials assembled to escort them, and the relevant offices provided banners and music.

sentences.zh: 是日，悉拜王府官屬，然未有府也，而選任冒濫，時不以為榮。

translations.literal: That day all were appointed to princely household offices—but there were as yet no actual princely establishments, and appointments were made with reckless indiscrimination; the age did not regard it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: That same day all were appointed to princely household offices—yet there were as yet no actual princely establishments, and appointments were made with reckless indiscrimination. The age did not regard it as an honor.

sentences.zh: 光王琚，開元十三年始王，與儀、潁、永、壽、延、盛、濟七王同封。

translations.literal: The Prince of Guang, Ju—in the thirteenth year of Kaiyuan was first enfeoffed, together with the seven princes of Yi, Ying, Yong, Shou, Yan, Sheng, and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Guang, Ju, was first enfeoffed in Kaiyuan 13, together with the seven princes of Yi, Ying, Yong, Shou, Yan, Sheng, and Ji.

sentences.zh: 俄領廣州都督。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he held the post of Military Governor of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he held the post of military governor of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 勇力善騎射，帝愛之。

translations.literal: Bold and strong, skilled in horsemanship and archery, he was beloved by the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Bold and strong, skilled in horsemanship and archery, he was beloved by the emperor.

sentences.zh: 與鄂王同居，友睦甚，皆篤學。

translations.literal: He lived together with the Prince of E in great friendship and mutual affection; both were devoted to learning.
translations.idiomatic: He lived together with the Prince of E in great friendship and mutual affection; both were devoted to learning.

sentences.zh: 既廢，無嗣。

translations.literal: After his deposition he left no heirs.
translations.idiomatic: After his deposition he left no heirs.

sentences.zh: 初，琚名涺，儀王濰，潁王沄，永王澤，壽王清，延王洄，盛王沐，濟王溢，信王沔，義王漼，陳王沚，豐王澄，恒王潓，涼王漎，汴王滔，至二十三年，詔悉改今名。

translations.literal: At the outset Ju was named Ti; the Prince of Ceremonial Rites was named Wei; the Prince of Ying was named Yun; the Prince of Yong was named Ze; the Prince of Shou was named Qing; the Prince of Yan was named Hui; the Prince of Sheng was named Mu; the Prince of Ji was named Yi; the Prince of Xin was named Mian; the Prince of Righteousness was named Cui; the Prince of Chen was named Chi; the Prince of Feng was named Cheng; the Prince of Heng was named Lian; the Prince of Liang was named Cong; the Prince of Bian was named Tao—by the twenty-third year an edict changed them all to their present names.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset Ju was named Ti; the Prince of Ceremonial Rites, Wei; the Prince of Ying, Yun; the Prince of Yong, Ze; the Prince of Shou, Qing; the Prince of Yan, Hui; the Prince of Sheng, Mu; the Prince of Ji, Yi; the Prince of Xin, Mian; the Prince of Righteousness, Cui; the Prince of Chen, Chi; the Prince of Feng, Cheng; the Prince of Heng, Lian; the Prince of Liang, Cong; and the Prince of Bian, Tao. By year 23 an edict changed them all to their present names.

sentences.zh: 夏悼王一，生韶秀，以母寵，故鐘愛，命之曰一。

translations.literal: Summer-Mourning Prince Yi was graceful and fair from birth. Because his mother was favored, he was deeply cherished, and the emperor named him One.
translations.idiomatic: Summer-Mourning Prince Yi was graceful and fair from birth. Because his mother was favored, he was deeply cherished, and the emperor named him One.

sentences.zh: 未免懷薨，追爵及謚。

translations.literal: He died before leaving the womb; posthumous rank and title were granted.
translations.idiomatic: He died before leaving the womb; posthumous rank and title were granted.

sentences.zh: 時帝在東都，故葬龍門東岑，欲宮中望見雲。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor was in the eastern capital, so the burial was at the eastern slope of Longmen, where the palace might look out and see the clouds above it.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the emperor was in the eastern capital, so the burial was placed on the eastern slope of Longmen, where the palace might look out and see the clouds above it.

sentences.zh: 儀王璲，即封，授河南牧。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yi, Xun—upon enfeoffment was appointed Governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yi, Xun, upon enfeoffment was appointed Governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈太傅。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously honored as Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously honored as Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 子侁王鐘陵郡，僆廣陵。

translations.literal: His son Shen was enfeoffed as Prince of Zhongling commandery; Mian as Prince of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shen was enfeoffed as Prince of Zhongling; Mian as Prince of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 懷思王敏，貌豐秀若圖畫，帝愛之。

translations.literal: Recalling-and-Thinking Prince Min was full-faced and handsome as if painted; the emperor loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Recalling-and-Thinking Prince Min was full-faced and handsome as if painted, and the emperor loved him.

sentences.zh: 甫晬薨，追爵及謚，祔葬敬陵。

translations.literal: He died just after his first birthday; posthumous rank and title were granted, and he was buried beside Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: He died just after his first birthday; posthumous rank and title were granted, and he was buried beside Jingling.

sentences.zh: 永王璘，少失母，肅宗自養視之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yong, Lin, lost his mother while young; Suzong himself raised and cared for him.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yong, Lin, lost his mother while young; Suzong himself raised and cared for him.

sentences.zh: 長聰敏好學。

translations.literal: Growing up he was clever and eager to learn.
translations.idiomatic: Growing up he was clever and eager to learn.

sentences.zh: 貌陋甚，不能正視。

translations.literal: His appearance was extremely ugly; he could not look people straight in the face.
translations.idiomatic: His appearance was extremely ugly; he could not look people straight in the face.

sentences.zh: 既封，領荊州大都督。

translations.literal: Once enfeoffed, he held the post of Grand Military Governor of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Once enfeoffed, he held the post of grand military governor of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，帝至扶風，詔璘即日赴鎮。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled and the emperor reached Fufeng, an edict ordered Lin to proceed to his post that very day.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled and the emperor reached Fufeng, an edict ordered Lin to proceed to his post that very day.

sentences.zh: 俄又領山南、江西、嶺南、黔中四道節度使，以少府監竇昭為副。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he also received the four circuit commissions of Shannan, Jiangxi, Lingnan, and Qianzhong, with Vice Minister of the Palace Storehouse Dou Zhao as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he also received commissions over the four circuits of Shannan, Jiangxi, Lingnan, and Qianzhong, with Dou Zhao, Vice Minister of the Palace Storehouse, as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 璘至江陵，募士得數萬，補署郎官、御史。

translations.literal: Lin reached Jiangling, recruited soldiers numbering in the tens of thousands, and appointed men to posts as court gentlemen and censors.
translations.idiomatic: Lin reached Jiangling, recruited soldiers numbering in the tens of thousands, and appointed men to posts as court gentlemen and censors.

sentences.zh: 時江淮租賦巨億萬，在所山委。

translations.literal: At the time the tax grain and levies of the Jiang-Huai region amounted to hundreds of millions; wherever stored, the piles rose like hills.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the tax grain and levies of the Jiang-Huai region amounted to hundreds of millions; wherever they were stored, the piles rose like hills.

sentences.zh: 璘生宮中，於事不通曉，見富且強，遂有窺江左意，以薛镠、李臺卿、韋子春、劉巨鱗、蔡F駉為謀主。

translations.literal: Lin had been born in the palace and understood nothing of practical affairs. Seeing such wealth and strength, he conceived a design on the lands south of the Yangzi, taking Xue Liu, Li Taiqing, Wei Zichun, Liu Julin, and Cai Bing as his chief advisers.
translations.idiomatic: Lin had been born in the palace and understood nothing of practical affairs. Seeing such wealth and strength, he conceived a design on the lands south of the Yangzi, taking Xue Liu, Li Taiqing, Wei Zichun, Liu Julin, and Cai Bing as his chief advisers.

sentences.zh: 肅宗聞之，詔璘還覲上皇於蜀，璘不從。

translations.literal: When Suzong learned of this, he ordered Lin to return and pay homage to the Retired Emperor in Shu; Lin did not obey.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong learned of this, he ordered Lin to return and pay homage to the Retired Emperor in Shu; Lin refused to obey.

sentences.zh: 其子襄城王亻易，剛鷙乏謀，亦樂亂，勸璘取金陵。

translations.literal: His son, the Prince of Xiangcheng, Ti, was fierce and overbearing but lacked strategy; he too delighted in disorder and urged Lin to seize Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: His son, the Prince of Xiangcheng, Ti, was fierce and overbearing but lacked strategy; he too delighted in disorder and urged Lin to seize Jinling.

sentences.zh: 即引舟師東下，甲士五千趨廣陵，以渾惟明、季廣琛、高仙琦為將，然未敢顯言取江左也。

translations.literal: Lin thereupon led his fleet eastward with five thousand armored soldiers hurrying toward Guangling, appointing Hun Weiming, Ji Guangchen, and Gao Xianqi as generals—yet he still did not dare openly speak of seizing the lands south of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Lin thereupon led his fleet eastward with five thousand armored soldiers hurrying toward Guangling, appointing Hun Weiming, Ji Guangchen, and Gao Xianqi as his generals—yet he still did not dare openly speak of seizing the lands south of the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 會吳郡采訪使李希言平牒璘，璘因發怒曰：「寡人上皇子，皇帝弟，地尊禮絕。

translations.literal: It happened that Li Xiyan, the surveillance commissioner of Wu commandery, sent Lin a letter on equal stationery. Lin grew angry and said: "I am a prince of the Retired Emperor, the emperor's younger brother—my rank is lofty and my ritual status singular.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Li Xiyan, the surveillance commissioner of Wu commandery, addressed Prince Lin in a letter on equal stationery—as though they were peers. Lin flew into a rage. "I am a prince of the Retired Emperor, the emperor's own younger brother," he said. "My rank is exalted and my ritual standing without equal.

sentences.zh: 今希言乃平牒抗威，落筆署字，何邪？

translations.literal: Now Xiyan sends a letter on equal stationery to assert authority, signing his name at the end—as though what?
translations.idiomatic: And now Xiyan dares send me a letter on equal footing, signing his name at the bottom as though he were my equal. What is the meaning of this?"

sentences.zh: 」乃使惟明襲希言，而令廣琛趨廣陵，攻采訪使李成式。

translations.literal: He thereupon sent Weiming to attack Xiyan, and ordered Guangchen to hurry to Guangling to assault the surveillance commissioner Li Chengshi.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon sent Hun Weiming to attack Xiyan and ordered Ji Guangchen to hurry to Guangling and assault the surveillance commissioner Li Chengshi.

sentences.zh: 璘至當塗，希言已屯丹楊，遣將元景曜等拒戰，不勝，降於璘，江淮震動。

translations.literal: Lin reached Dangtu. Xiyan had already encamped at Danyang and sent generals including Yuan Jingyao to resist; they were defeated and surrendered to Lin, and the Jiang-Huai region was shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Lin reached Dangtu. Xiyan had already encamped at Danyang and sent generals including Yuan Jingyao to resist, but they were defeated and surrendered to Lin. The entire Jiang-Huai region was shaken.

sentences.zh: 明年，肅宗遣宦者啖廷瑤等與成式謀招喻之。

translations.literal: The next year, Suzong sent the eunuch Kan Tingyao and others to join Chengshi in plotting to win Lin over by persuasion.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Emperor Suzong sent the eunuch Kan Tingyao and others to join Li Chengshi in a plan to win Lin over through persuasion.

sentences.zh: 時河北招討判官李銑在廣陵，有兵千余，廷瑤邀銑屯揚子，成式又遣裴戎以廣陵卒三千戍伊婁埭，張旗幟，大閱士。

translations.literal: At the time Li Xian, adjutant of the Hebei recruitment campaign, was at Guangling with more than a thousand troops. Tingyao invited Xian to encamp at Yangzi. Chengshi also sent Pei Rong with three thousand Guangling soldiers to garrison Yilou Dam, raising banners and conducting a grand review of troops.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Li Xian, adjutant on the Hebei recruitment staff, was at Guangling with more than a thousand troops. Tingyao invited Xian to encamp at Yangzi. Chengshi also sent Pei Rong with three thousand Guangling soldiers to garrison Yilou Dam, raising banners and putting the men through a grand review.

sentences.zh: 璘與亻易登陴望之，有懼色。

translations.literal: Lin and Ti climbed the battlements to look out and showed fear on their faces.
translations.idiomatic: Lin and his son Ti climbed the battlements to look out and could not hide the fear on their faces.

sentences.zh: 廣琛知事不集，謂諸將曰：「與公等從王，豈欲反邪？

translations.literal: Guangchen knew matters would not succeed and said to the generals: "When I followed the prince with you, did I intend to rebel?
translations.idiomatic: Guangchen knew the enterprise was doomed. He said to the other generals, "When I followed the prince here with all of you, did any of us mean to rebel?

sentences.zh: 上皇播遷，道路不通，而諸子無賢於王者。

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor is wandering in exile and the roads are blocked, and among the sons none is worthier than our prince.
translations.idiomatic: The Retired Emperor wanders in exile and the roads are cut off, yet among the imperial sons none is worthier than our prince.

sentences.zh: 如總江淮銳兵，長驅雍、洛，大功可成。

translations.literal: If we gathered the elite troops of the Jiang-Huai and drove straight for Yong and Luo, a great achievement could be accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Had we gathered the elite troops of the Jiang-Huai and driven straight for Yong and Luo, a great achievement might still have been within reach.

sentences.zh: 今乃不然，使吾等名絓叛逆，如後世何？

translations.literal: Now it is not so—we are being made to bear the stain of rebel names. What shall we say to posterity?
translations.idiomatic: Instead we are being branded rebels. What account shall we give to posterity?"

sentences.zh: 」眾許諾，遂割臂盟。

translations.literal: The host assented and they cut their arms to swear alliance.
translations.idiomatic: The men agreed. They cut their arms and swore a blood oath.

sentences.zh: 於是惟明奔江寧，馮季康奔白沙，廣琛以兵六千奔廣陵。

translations.literal: Thereupon Weiming fled to Jiangning, Feng Jikang fled to Baisha, and Guangchen led six thousand troops to Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Weiming fled to Jiangning, Feng Jikang fled to Baisha, and Guangchen led six thousand troops toward Guangling.

sentences.zh: 璘使騎追躡之，廣琛曰：「我德王，故不忍決戰，逃命歸國耳。

translations.literal: Lin sent horsemen to pursue him. Guangchen said: "I owe the prince a debt of gratitude, so I would not bring myself to fight a decisive battle—I am only fleeing to save my life and return to the state."
translations.idiomatic: Lin sent cavalry in pursuit. Guangchen said, "I owe the prince a debt of gratitude, so I could not bring myself to fight a decisive battle. I am only fleeing to save my life and return to the empire."

sentences.zh: 若逼我，且決死。

translations.literal: If you press me, I will fight to the death.
translations.idiomatic: But if you press me, I will fight to the death."

sentences.zh: 」追者止，乃免。

translations.literal: The pursuers halted, and he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuers halted, and he got away.

sentences.zh: 是夜，銑陣江北，夜然束葦，人執二炬，景亂水中，覘者以倍告，璘軍亦舉火應之。

translations.literal: That night Xian arrayed his troops north of the river. At night they lit bundles of reeds, each man holding two torches; the scene was confused upon the water. Observers reported the force doubled; Lin's army also raised fires in response.
translations.idiomatic: That night Xian drew up his troops north of the river. After dark they lit bundles of reeds, each man holding two torches until the river glittered with confused light. Scouts reported that the enemy force had doubled; Lin's army too lit fires in reply.

sentences.zh: 璘疑王師已濟，攜兒女及麾下遁去。

translations.literal: Lin suspected the imperial army had already crossed and fled with his women, children, and followers.
translations.idiomatic: Lin suspected the imperial army had already crossed the river and fled with his wives, children, and followers.

sentences.zh: 遲明覺其紿，復入城，具舟楫，使亻易驅眾趨晉陵。

translations.literal: At dawn he realized he had been deceived, re-entered the city, prepared boats, and sent Ti to drive the host toward Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he realized he had been tricked. He re-entered the city, fitted out boats, and sent Ti to drive the host toward Jinling.

sentences.zh: 諜者告曰：「王走矣！

translations.literal: Spies reported: "The prince has fled!"
translations.idiomatic: Spies reported, "The prince has fled!"

sentences.zh: 」成式以兵進，先鋒至新豐，璘使亻易、仙琦逆擊之。

translations.literal: Chengshi advanced with troops. The vanguard reached Xinfeng. Lin sent Ti and Xianqi to meet the attack.
translations.idiomatic: Chengshi advanced with his army. When the vanguard reached Xinfeng, Lin sent Ti and Gao Xianqi to meet the attack.

sentences.zh: 銑合勢，張左右翼，射亻易中肩，軍遂敗。

translations.literal: Xian combined forces, deployed both wings, and shot Ti in the shoulder; the army was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Xian combined his forces, deployed both wings, and shot Ti in the shoulder. Lin's army broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 仙琦與璘奔鄱陽，司馬閉城拒，璘怒，焚城門入之，收庫兵，掠余幹，將南走嶺外。

translations.literal: Xianqi and Lin fled to Poyang. The prefect closed the city gates to resist. Enraged, Lin burned the city gate to enter, seized the arsenal weapons, plundered Yugan, and prepared to flee south beyond the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Xianqi and Lin fled to Poyang. The prefect closed the gates against them. Enraged, Lin burned the gate to force his way in, seized the weapons in the arsenal, plundered Yugan, and prepared to flee south beyond the mountain passes.

sentences.zh: 皇甫侁兵追及之，戰大庾嶺，璘中矢被執，侁殺之。

translations.literal: Huangfu Shen's troops caught up with them and fought at Dayu Ridge. Lin was struck by an arrow, captured, and Shen killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Shen's troops caught up with them and fought at Dayu Ridge. Lin was struck by an arrow, captured, and Shen killed him.

sentences.zh: 亻易為亂兵所害，仙琦逃去。

translations.literal: Ti was killed by disorderly soldiers; Xianqi escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Ti was killed by rampaging soldiers. Xianqi escaped.

sentences.zh: 璘未敗時，上皇下誥：「降為庶人，徙置房陵。

translations.literal: Before Lin was defeated, the Retired Emperor issued a proclamation: "Strip him of rank and make him a commoner; relocate him to Fangling."
translations.idiomatic: Before Lin's defeat, the Retired Emperor had issued a proclamation: "Strip him of rank and reduce him to commoner status; relocate him to Fangling."

sentences.zh: 」及死，侁送妻子至蜀，上皇傷悼久之。

translations.literal: After his death Shen sent his wife and children to Shu; the Retired Emperor mourned them for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: After Lin's death Shen sent his wife and children to Shu. The Retired Emperor grieved for a long time.

sentences.zh: 肅宗以少所自鞠，不宣其罪。

translations.literal: Suzong, having raised him from childhood himself, did not publicly announce his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong, who had raised Lin from childhood, did not publicly proclaim his crimes.

sentences.zh: 謂左右曰：「皇甫侁執吾弟，不送之蜀而擅殺之，何邪？

translations.literal: He said to those around him: "Huangfu Shen seized my younger brother, failed to send him to Shu, and killed him on his own authority—why?"
translations.idiomatic: He said to those around him, "Huangfu Shen seized my younger brother, failed to send him to Shu, and killed him on his own authority. What was he thinking?"

sentences.zh: 」由是不復用。

translations.literal: For this reason Shen was never again employed.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason Huangfu Shen was never again employed.

sentences.zh: 薛寔等皆伏誅。

translations.literal: Xue Shi and the others were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Shi and the others were all put to death.

sentences.zh: 子儹為余姚王，偵莒國公，儇郕國公，伶、儀並國子祭酒。

translations.literal: His sons: Yi was Prince of Yuyao; Zhen, Duke of Ju; Xuan, Duke of Bi; Ling and Yi both became Directors of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Lin's sons: Yi was enfeoffed as Prince of Yuyao; Zhen as Duke of Ju; Xuan as Duke of Bi; Ling and Yi both became Directors of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 壽王瑁，母惠妃頻姙不育，及瑁生，寧王請養邸中，元妃自乳之，名為己子，故封比諸王最後。

translations.literal: Prince Shou Mao: his mother Consort Hui had been pregnant many times without successful births. When Mao was born, the Prince of Ning asked to raise him in his residence; the Primary Consort nursed him herself and treated him as her own son, so his enfeoffment came last among the princes.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shou Mao's mother, Consort Hui, had been pregnant many times without bringing a child safely to term. When Mao was born, the Prince of Ning asked to raise him in his own residence. The Primary Consort nursed the boy herself and treated him as her own son, and for this reason his enfeoffment came last among the princes.

sentences.zh: 開元十五年，遙領益州大都督。

translations.literal: In Kaiyuan 15 he held the titular post of Grand Military Governor of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 15 he held the titular post of grand military governor of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 初，帝以永王等尚幼，詔不入謁。

translations.literal: At first the emperor, because Yong Wang and the others were still young, decreed they should not enter for audiences.
translations.idiomatic: At first, because Yong Wang and the other princes were still young, the emperor decreed that they should not enter for imperial audiences.

sentences.zh: 瑁七歲，請與諸兄眾謝，拜舞有儀矩，帝異之。

translations.literal: When Mao was seven he requested to join his elder brothers in paying thanks; his bowing and dancing were marked by proper ritual, and the emperor was struck by it.
translations.idiomatic: When Mao was seven he asked to join his elder brothers in paying formal thanks. His bowing and dancing were executed with proper ritual grace, and the emperor was deeply impressed.

sentences.zh: 寧王薨，請制服以報私恩，詔可。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Ning died, he requested to wear mourning to repay a private debt of kindness; the decree approved.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Ning died, Mao requested permission to wear mourning in repayment of a private debt of kindness. The emperor granted his request.

sentences.zh: 大歷十年薨，贈太傅。

translations.literal: He died in Dali 10 and was posthumously honored as Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Dali 10 and was posthumously honored as Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 子王者三人，僾王德陽郡，伓濟陽郡，偡廣陽郡，伉薛國公，傑國子祭酒。

translations.literal: Three of his sons received princely titles: Yi, Prince of Deyang; Pi, Prince of Jiyang; Ting, Prince of Guangyang. Kang was Duke of Xue; Jie, Director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Three of his sons received princely titles: Yi as Prince of Deyang, Pi as Prince of Jiyang, and Ting as Prince of Guangyang. Kang was created Duke of Xue, and Jie became Director of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 盛宣王琦，既封，領揚州大都督。

translations.literal: Sheng Xuan Wang Qi, once enfeoffed, held the post of Grand Military Governor of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Xuan Wang Qi, once enfeoffed, held the post of grand military governor of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝之西，詔為廣陵大都督、淮南江東河南節度大使，以劉匯為副，李成式為副大使，琦不行。

translations.literal: When the emperor went west, Qi was ordered Grand Military Governor of Guangling and Grand Military Commissioner of Huainan, Jiangdong, and Henan, with Liu Hui as deputy and Li Chengshi as deputy commissioner; Qi did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor moved west, Qi was ordered to serve as grand military governor of Guangling and grand military commissioner over Huainan, Jiangdong, and Henan, with Liu Hui as deputy and Li Chengshi as deputy commissioner. Qi did not take up the post.

sentences.zh: 廣德二年薨，贈太傅。

translations.literal: He died in Guangde 2 and was posthumously honored as Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Guangde 2 and was posthumously honored as Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 子償封真定王，佩武都王，俗徐國公，系許國公。

translations.literal: His sons: Chang was enfeoffed Prince of Zhending; Pei, Prince of Wudu; Su, Duke of Xu; Xi, Duke of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: His sons: Chang was enfeoffed as Prince of Zhending; Pei as Prince of Wudu; Su as Duke of Xu; and Xi as Duke of Xu.

sentences.zh: 濟王環，逸其薨年。

translations.literal: Prince Ji Huan—the year of his death is not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ji Huan—the year of his death is not recorded.

sentences.zh: 子傃王永嘉郡，俛平樂郡。

translations.literal: His sons: Su, Prince of Yongjia; Mian, Prince of Pingle.
translations.idiomatic: His sons: Su was Prince of Yongjia, and Mian was Prince of Pingle.

sentences.zh: 信王瑝，開元二十一年始王，與義、陳、豐、恒、涼、汴六王同封。

translations.literal: Prince Xin Huang—in Kaiyuan 21 he was first enfeoffed, together with the six princes of Yi, Chen, Feng, Heng, Liang, and Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xin Huang was first enfeoffed in Kaiyuan 21, together with the six princes of Yi, Chen, Feng, Heng, Liang, and Bian.

sentences.zh: 子佟封新安王，倜晉陵王。

translations.literal: His sons: Tong was enfeoffed Prince of Xin'an; Ti, Prince of Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: His sons: Tong was enfeoffed as Prince of Xin'an, and Ti as Prince of Jinling.

sentences.zh: 義王玼，與信王並失薨年。

translations.literal: Prince Yi Ci, together with Prince Xin, lacks a recorded year of death.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yi Ci, like Prince Xin, has no recorded year of death.

sentences.zh: 子儀為舞陽王，僇高密王。

translations.literal: His sons: Yi, Prince of Wuyang; Lu, Prince of Gaomi.
translations.idiomatic: His sons: Yi was Prince of Wuyang, and Lu was Prince of Gaomi.

sentences.zh: 陳王珪，二十一子，得王者三人，倫王安南郡，佗臨淮，佼安陽。

translations.literal: Prince Chen Gui had twenty-one sons; three received princely titles: Lun, Prince of An'nan; Tuo, Prince of Linhuai; Jiao, Prince of Anyang.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Chen Gui had twenty-one sons. Three received princely titles: Lun as Prince of An'nan, Tuo as Prince of Linhuai, and Jiao as Prince of Anyang.

sentences.zh: 豐王珙，已封，為左衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Prince Feng Gong, already enfeoffed, served as General-in-Chief of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Feng Gong, already enfeoffed, served as General-in-Chief of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 帝至普安，授珙武威都督、河西隴右安西北庭節度大使，以隴西太守鄧景山為副，珙不行。

translations.literal: When the emperor reached Pu'an, Gong was appointed Military Governor of Wuwei and Grand Military Commissioner of Hexi, Longxi, Anxi, and Beiting, with Deng Jingshan, Administrator of Longxi, as deputy; Gong did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor reached Pu'an, Gong was appointed military governor of Wuwei and grand military commissioner over Hexi, Longxi, Anxi, and Beiting, with Deng Jingshan, administrator of Longxi, as his deputy. Gong did not take up the commission.

sentences.zh: 廣德初，吐蕃入京師，代宗幸陜，將軍王懷忠閉苑門，以五百騎劫諸王西迎虜，遇郭子儀，懷忠曰：「上東遷，宗社無主，今仆奉諸王西奔，以系天下望。

translations.literal: In early Guangde, when Tibetans entered the capital and Emperor Daizong fled to Shan, General Wang Huaizhong closed the park gates and with five hundred cavalry abducted the princes westward to welcome the invaders. He met Guo Ziyi. Huaizhong said: "The emperor has moved east; the altars of state are without a master. Now I, your servant, am leading the princes west to sustain the hopes of the empire."
translations.idiomatic: In early Guangde, when Tibetans entered the capital and Emperor Daizong fled to Shan, General Wang Huaizhong closed the park gates and, with five hundred cavalry, seized the princes and drove them west to welcome the invaders. He met Guo Ziyi and said, "The emperor has moved east and the altars of state stand without a master. I am now leading the princes west to sustain the empire's hopes.

sentences.zh: 公為元帥，惟所廢置。

translations.literal: You are the grand marshal—you may install or remove whomever you choose."
translations.idiomatic: You are the grand marshal. Install or remove whomever you will."

sentences.zh: 」子儀未對。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi made no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi made no reply.

sentences.zh: 珙輒曰：「公何如？

translations.literal: Gong immediately said: "What about you, sir?"
translations.idiomatic: Gong immediately said, "What about you, sir?"

sentences.zh: 」司馬王延昌質責珙曰：「上雖蒙塵，未有失德，王為籓翰，安得狂悖之言？

translations.literal: Sima Wang Yanchang sternly rebuked Gong: "Though the emperor is covered in dust, he has committed no misdeed. As a frontier prince, how can you speak such reckless words?"
translations.idiomatic: Sima Wang Yanchang sternly rebuked Gong. "Though the emperor is covered in the dust of exile, he has committed no misdeed. As a frontier prince, how dare you speak such reckless words?"

sentences.zh: 」子儀亦讓之，即護送行在所，帝赦不責。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi also reproved him and at once escorted them to the emperor's traveling court; the emperor pardoned them without punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi reproved him as well and at once escorted the princes to the emperor's traveling court. The emperor pardoned them without punishment.

sentences.zh: 珙語不遜，群臣恐其亂，請除之，乃賜死。

translations.literal: Gong's words were insubordinate; the ministers feared he would cause disorder and requested his removal; he was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: Gong's words had been insubordinate. The ministers feared he would stir up disorder and requested his removal. He was granted death.

sentences.zh: 子佻為齊安王。

translations.literal: His son Tiao was Prince of Qi'an.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tiao was enfeoffed as Prince of Qi'an.

sentences.zh: 恒王瑱，好方士，常服道士服。

translations.literal: Prince Heng Tian loved Daoist masters and often wore Daoist robes.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Heng Tian loved Daoist masters and often wore Daoist robes.

sentences.zh: 從帝幸蜀，還，代宗時薨。

translations.literal: He accompanied the emperor to Shu and returned; he died in the time of Daizong.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor to Shu and returned. He died during the reign of Emperor Daizong.

sentences.zh: 涼王璿，母高平王重規之女，宮中號小武妃者。

translations.literal: Prince Liang Xuan: his mother was a daughter of the Prince of Gaoping Chonggui, known within the palace as Little Consort Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Liang Xuan's mother was a daughter of the Prince of Gaoping, Chonggui, known within the palace as Little Consort Wu.

sentences.zh: 璿薨代宗時。

translations.literal: Xuan died in the time of Daizong.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan died during the reign of Emperor Daizong.

sentences.zh: 子仂為瀘陽郡王。

translations.literal: His son Le was Prince of Luyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Le was enfeoffed as Prince of Luyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 唐制：親王封戶八百，增至千；

translations.literal: Tang institutions: for princes of the blood, the enfeoffment households numbered eight hundred, increased to one thousand;
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang institutions, princes of the blood received eight hundred enfeoffment households, increased in some cases to one thousand;

sentences.zh: 公主三百，長公主止六百。

translations.literal: for princesses three hundred; for senior princesses no more than six hundred.
translations.idiomatic: princesses received three hundred, and senior princesses no more than six hundred.

sentences.zh: 高宗時，沛英豫三王、太平公主武後所生，戶始逾制，垂拱中，太平至千二百戶。

translations.literal: In Gaozong's time the three princes of Pei, Ying, and Yu and Princess Taiping, born of Empress Wu, first exceeded the quota; in the Zhonggu reign Princess Taiping reached twelve hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In Gaozong's time the three princes of Pei, Ying, and Yu and Princess Taiping, all born of Empress Wu, first exceeded the prescribed quotas. In the Zhonggu reign Princess Taiping's allotment reached twelve hundred households.

sentences.zh: 聖歷初，相王、太平皆三千，壽春等五王各三百。

translations.literal: In early Shengli, the Prince of Xiang and Princess Taiping each had three thousand; the five princes including Shouchun had three hundred each.
translations.idiomatic: In early Shengli the Prince of Xiang and Princess Taiping each received three thousand households, while the five princes including Shouchun received three hundred each.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，相王、太平至五千，衛王三千，溫王二千，壽春等王皆七百，嗣雍、衡陽、臨淄、巴陵、中山王五百，安樂公主二千，長寧千五百，宣城、宜城、宣安各千，相王女為縣主，各三百。

translations.literal: In early Shenlong, the Prince of Xiang and Princess Taiping reached five thousand; Prince Wei three thousand; Prince Wen two thousand; the Shouchun princes seven hundred each; the princes of Siyong, Hengyang, Linzi, Baling, and Zhongshan five hundred each; Princess Anle two thousand; Changning fifteen hundred; Xuancheng, Yicheng, and Xu'an a thousand each; the Prince of Xiang's daughters as chieflets three hundred each.
translations.idiomatic: In early Shenlong the Prince of Xiang and Princess Taiping reached five thousand households; Prince Wei three thousand; Prince Wen two thousand; the Shouchun princes seven hundred each; the princes of Siyong, Hengyang, Linzi, Baling, and Zhongshan five hundred each; Princess Anle two thousand; Changning fifteen hundred; Xuancheng, Yicheng, and Xu'an a thousand each; and the Prince of Xiang's daughters, enfeoffed as chieflets, three hundred each.

sentences.zh: 相王增至七千，安樂三千，長寧二千五百，宜城以下二千。

translations.literal: The Prince of Xiang was increased to seven thousand; Anle to three thousand; Changning to twenty-five hundred; Yicheng and below to two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Xiang was later increased to seven thousand households; Princess Anle to three thousand; Changning to twenty-five hundred; and Yicheng and the rest to two thousand.

sentences.zh: 相王、太平、長寧、安樂以七丁為限，雖水旱不蠲，以國租、庸滿之。

translations.literal: For the Prince of Xiang, Taiping, Changning, and Anle the limit was seven retainers per household; even in flood or drought this was not remitted—it was made up from state land tax and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: For the Prince of Xiang, Taiping, Changning, and Anle the limit was seven retainers per household. Even in years of flood or drought this quota was not remitted; it was made up from state land tax and corvée payments.

sentences.zh: 中宗遺詔，雍、壽春王進為親王，戶千。

translations.literal: In Zhongzong's death edict, the princes of Yong and Shouchun were advanced to princes of the first rank with one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongzong's death edict the princes of Yong and Shouchun were advanced to princes of the first rank, each with one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 開元後，天子敦睦兄弟，故寧王戶至五千五百，岐、薛五千，申王以外家微，戶四千，邠王千八百，帝妹戶千，中宗諸女如之，通以三丁為限。

translations.literal: After Kaiyuan the Son of Heaven cherished brotherly harmony, so the Prince of Ning reached fifty-five hundred households, Qi and Xue five thousand each; Prince Shen, on account of his mother's low birth, four thousand; Prince Bin eighteen hundred; the emperor's sisters a thousand each; Zhongzong's daughters likewise—all with a general limit of three retainers per household.
translations.idiomatic: After Kaiyuan the Son of Heaven cultivated brotherly harmony among the princes, so the Prince of Ning reached fifty-five hundred households, Qi and Xue five thousand each, Prince Shen four thousand on account of his mother's humble birth, Prince Bin eighteen hundred, the emperor's sisters a thousand each, and Zhongzong's daughters likewise—all subject to a general limit of three retainers per household.

sentences.zh: 及皇子封王，戶二千，公主五百。

translations.literal: When imperial sons were enfeoffed as princes, households numbered two thousand; princesses five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: When imperial sons were enfeoffed as princes they received two thousand households; princesses received five hundred.

sentences.zh: 咸宜公主以母惠妃故，封至千，自是，諸公主例千戶止。

translations.literal: Princess Xianyi, because her mother was Consort Hui, received one thousand—thereafter princesses were capped at one thousand households as a rule.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Xianyi, because her mother was Consort Hui, received one thousand households. Thereafter princesses were as a rule capped at one thousand.

sentences.zh: 初，文德皇后崩，晉王最幼，太宗憐之，不使出閤。

translations.literal: At first, after Empress Wende died, the Prince of Jin was youngest; Taizong pitied him and did not allow him to leave the Inner Quarters.
translations.idiomatic: At first, after Empress Wende died, the Prince of Jin was the youngest child. Taizong pitied him and would not allow him to leave the Inner Quarters.

sentences.zh: 豫王亦以武後少子不出閤，嗣聖初，即帝位，及降封相王，乃出閤。

translations.literal: Prince Yu likewise, as Empress Wu's youngest son, did not leave the Inner Quarters; in early Sisheng he ascended the throne, and only when he was demoted to Prince of Xiang did he leave the Inner Quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yu likewise, as Empress Wu's youngest son, did not leave the Inner Quarters. In early Sisheng he ascended the throne, and only when he was later demoted to Prince of Xiang did he leave the Inner Quarters.

sentences.zh: 中宗時，譙王失愛，遷外籓，溫王年十七，猶居宮中，遂立為帝。

translations.literal: In Zhongzong's time Prince Qiao lost favor and was moved to an outer fief; Prince Wen at seventeen still lived in the palace and was thereupon installed as emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongzong's time Prince Qiao lost favor and was transferred to an outer fief. Prince Wen, at seventeen, still lived within the palace and was thereupon installed as emperor.

sentences.zh: 開元後，皇子幼，多居禁內，既長，詔附苑城為大宮，分院而處，號「十王宅」，所謂慶、忠、棣、鄂、榮、光、儀、潁、永、延、盛、濟等王，以十，舉全數也。

translations.literal: After Kaiyuan, imperial sons when young mostly lived within the Forbidden Inner; once grown, an edict ordered pavilions built against the park wall as a great palace, divided into courtyards—the "Ten Princes' Residence," comprising the princes of Qing, Zhong, Di, E, Rong, Guang, Yi, Ying, Yong, Yan, Sheng, Ji, and others; the ten is a round number.
translations.idiomatic: After Kaiyuan, imperial sons in youth mostly lived within the Forbidden Inner. Once they had grown, an edict ordered pavilions built against the park wall as a great palace, divided into separate courtyards—the Ten Princes' Residence, housing the princes of Qing, Zhong, Di, E, Rong, Guang, Yi, Ying, Yong, Yan, Sheng, Ji, and others. The ten is a round number for the whole.

sentences.zh: 中人押之，就夾城參天子起居。

translations.literal: Eunuchs supervised them; through the walled passage they attended the Son of Heaven's daily movements.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs supervised them, and through the walled passage they attended the Son of Heaven's daily movements.

sentences.zh: 家令日進膳。

translations.literal: The Director of the Household provided daily meals.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Household saw to their daily meals.

sentences.zh: 引詞學士入授書，謂之侍讀。

translations.literal: Literary scholars were brought in to teach—these were called Readers-in-Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Literary scholars were brought in to instruct them. These tutors were called Readers-in-Attendance.

sentences.zh: 壽、信、義、陳、豐、恒、涼七王就封，亦居十宅。

translations.literal: The seven princes Shou, Xin, Yi, Chen, Feng, Heng, and Liang, though enfeoffed, also dwelt in the Ten Princes' Residence.
translations.idiomatic: The seven princes Shou, Xin, Yi, Chen, Feng, Heng, and Liang, though already enfeoffed, also dwelt in the Ten Princes' Residence.

sentences.zh: 鄂、光廢死，忠王立為太子，慶、棣繼薨，唯榮、儀十四王居院，而府幕列於外坊，歲時通名起居。

translations.literal: E and Guang were deposed and died; Zhong was established as crown prince; Qing and Di died in succession—only Rong, Yi, and fourteen princes remained in the courtyards, with their staff offices arrayed in outer wards; at the seasons they sent names and greetings.
translations.idiomatic: E and Guang were deposed and died. Zhong was established as crown prince. Qing and Di died in succession. Only Rong, Yi, and fourteen princes remained in the courtyards, while their staff offices were arrayed in outer wards. At the seasonal observances they sent their names and greetings.

sentences.zh: 既又諸孫多，則於宅外更置「百孫院」。

translations.literal: As imperial grandsons also grew numerous, outside the residence they further established the "Hundred Grandsons' Courtyard."
translations.idiomatic: As imperial grandsons also grew numerous, a Hundred Grandsons' Courtyard was established outside the residence.

sentences.zh: 天子歲幸華清宮，又置十王、百孫院於宮側。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven went each year to Huaqing Palace, Ten Princes' and Hundred Grandsons' courtyards were also set up beside the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the Son of Heaven went each year to Huaqing Palace, Ten Princes' and Hundred Grandsons' courtyards were also set up beside the palace.

sentences.zh: 宮人每院四百余，百孫院亦三四十人。

translations.literal: Palace women in each courtyard numbered more than four hundred; the Hundred Grandsons' Courtyard also thirty or forty.
translations.idiomatic: Palace women in each courtyard numbered more than four hundred; in the Hundred Grandsons' Courtyard there were also thirty or forty.

sentences.zh: 禁中置維城庫，以給諸王月奉。

translations.literal: Within the Forbidden Inner a Weicheng Storehouse was established to supply the princes' monthly stipends.
translations.idiomatic: Within the Forbidden Inner a Weicheng Storehouse was established to supply the princes' monthly stipends.

sentences.zh: 諸孫納妃、嫁女，就十王宅。

translations.literal: When grandsons took brides or daughters were married, the ceremonies were held at the Ten Princes' Residence.
translations.idiomatic: When grandsons took brides or daughters were given in marriage, the ceremonies were held at the Ten Princes' Residence.

sentences.zh: 太子不居東宮，處乘輿所幸別院。

translations.literal: The crown prince did not dwell in the Eastern Palace but in whatever separate courtyard the imperial carriage favored.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince did not dwell in the Eastern Palace but in whichever separate courtyard the imperial carriage happened to favor.

sentences.zh: 太子、親王、公主婚嫁並供帳於崇仁之禮院。

translations.literal: Crown princes, princes of the blood, and princesses all had wedding pavilions supplied at the Ch'ung-jen Ceremonial Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Crown princes, princes of the blood, and princesses all had their wedding pavilions supplied at the Ch'ung-jen Ceremonial Hall.

sentences.zh: 此承平制雲。

translations.literal: Such were the institutions of peace.
translations.idiomatic: Such were the institutions of an age of peace.

sentences.zh: 肅宗十四子：章敬皇后生代宗皇帝，宮人孫生系，張生倓，王生佖，陳婕妤生僅，韋妃生 ，張美人生侹，後宮生榮，裴昭儀生僙，段婕妤生倕，崔妃生偲，張皇后生佋，侗，後宮生僖。

translations.literal: Suzong's fourteen sons: Empress Zhangjing bore Emperor Daizong; palace woman Sun bore Xi; Zhang bore Tan; Wang bore Bi; Lady Chen bore Jin; Consort Wei bore Xian; Lady Zhang the Fair bore Bing; the inner palace bore Rong; Lady Pei bore Huang; Lady Duan bore Chui; Consort Cui bore Si; Empress Zhang bore Zhao and Tong; the inner palace bore Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong had fourteen sons. Empress Zhangjing bore Emperor Daizong. The palace woman Sun bore Xi; Zhang bore Tan; Wang bore Bi. Lady Chen bore Jin; Consort Wei bore Xian; Lady Zhang the Fair bore Bing. The inner palace bore Rong. Lady Pei bore Huang; Lady Duan bore Chui; Consort Cui bore Si. Empress Zhang bore Zhao and Tong. The inner palace bore Xi.

sentences.zh: 越王系，生開元時。

translations.literal: Prince Yue Xi was born in the Kaiyuan period.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yue Xi was born during the Kaiyuan period.

sentences.zh: 玄宗末年，悉王太子子，故系王南陽郡。

translations.literal: Near the end of Xuanzong's reign all princes' sons were enfeoffed, so Xi was made Prince of Nanyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Xuanzong's reign all sons of princes were enfeoffed, and Xi was made Prince of Nanyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 帝即位，至德二載十二月，進王趙，與彭、兗、涇、鄆、襄、杞、召、興、定九王同封。

translations.literal: When the emperor ascended the throne, in the twelfth month of Zhide 2 Xi was advanced to Prince of Zhao, enfeoffed together with the nine princes Peng, Yan, Jing, Yun, Xiang, Qi, Zhao, Xing, and Ding.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor ascended the throne, in the twelfth month of Zhide 2 Xi was advanced to Prince of Zhao and enfeoffed together with the nine princes Peng, Yan, Jing, Yun, Xiang, Qi, Zhao, Xing, and Ding.

sentences.zh: 乾元二年，九節度兵潰河北，朝廷震駭，乃以李光弼代郭子儀總兵關東，而光弼請賢王為帥，於是詔系充天下兵馬元帥，而光弼以司空兼侍中、薊國公副，知節度行營事，系留京師。

translations.literal: In Qianyuan 2, the troops of nine military commissioners collapsed in Hebei and the court was shaken. Li Guangbi replaced Guo Ziyi to command armies east of the Pass. Guangbi requested a worthy prince as commander; an edict made Xi Grand Marshal of All Armies under Heaven, with Guangbi as deputy in his capacity as Minister of Works and Concurrent Palace Attendant, Duke of Ji, managing the circuit headquarters in the field—while Xi remained in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianyuan 2 the troops of nine military commissioners collapsed in Hebei and the court was shaken. Li Guangbi replaced Guo Ziyi to command the armies east of the Pass. Guangbi requested a worthy prince as supreme commander. An edict appointed Xi Grand Marshal of All Armies under Heaven, with Guangbi serving as deputy in his capacity as Minister of Works, Concurrent Palace Attendant, and Duke of Ji, managing the circuit headquarters in the field, while Xi remained in the capital.

sentences.zh: 史思明陷洛陽，系請行，不聽。

translations.literal: When Shi Siming took Luoyang, Xi requested to take the field; his request was denied.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Siming took Luoyang, Xi requested permission to take the field. His request was denied.

sentences.zh: 明年，徙王越。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Prince of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was transferred to Prince of Yue.

sentences.zh: 帝寢疾，皇太子監國，張皇后與中人李輔國有隙，因召太子入，謂曰：「輔國典禁軍，用事久，四方詔令皆出其口，矯天子制，逼徙聖皇，天下側目。

translations.literal: The emperor lay ill in bed; the crown prince supervised the realm. Empress Zhang had a rift with the eunuch Li Fuguo. She summoned the crown prince and said: 'Fuguo commands the forbidden armies and has held power long. Edicts from the four quarters all issue from his mouth. He forged the Son of Heaven's orders and forced the relocation of the Sacred Emperor—the world watched with sidelong eyes.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor lay gravely ill, and the crown prince governed in his stead. Empress Zhang had fallen out with the eunuch Li Fuguo. She summoned the crown prince and said, 'Fuguo commands the palace guard and has wielded power for years. Every edict in the realm passes his lips. He forged the emperor's commands and drove the retired sovereign from the capital—the court and people watched him in fear.'

sentences.zh: 今上疾彌留，輔國常怏怏，忌吾與汝。

translations.literal: Now the sovereign's illness lingers at death's door; Fuguo is often sullen and bears resentment toward me and you.
translations.idiomatic: Now His Majesty's illness deepens by the hour. Fuguo grows sullen and resentful—and he hates us both.

sentences.zh: 又程元振陰結黃門，圖不軌。

translations.literal: Moreover Cheng Yuanzhen secretly joins with the Yellow Gate, plotting treason.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yuanzhen has been secretly colluding with the inner palace, scheming rebellion.

sentences.zh: 若釋不誅，禍不移頃。

translations.literal: If we release them without executing them, disaster will not wait a moment.
translations.idiomatic: If we spare them and do not strike first, ruin will come in no time at all.'

sentences.zh: 」太子泣曰：「此二人者，陛下勛舊，而上體不豫，重以此事，得無震驚乎？

translations.literal: The crown prince wept and said: 'These two men are Your Majesty's meritorious veterans, and the sovereign's body is unwell—would not such a matter surely shock him?'
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince wept and said, 'These two served the late emperor with distinction, and Father is already so ill—would this not shock him to his core?'

sentences.zh: 願出外徐計之。

translations.literal: I wish to go outside and consider the matter slowly.
translations.idiomatic: Let me withdraw and plan this with care.'

sentences.zh: 」後曰：「是難與共事者！

translations.literal: The empress said: 'These are men difficult to work with!'
translations.idiomatic: The empress said, 'Men like these are impossible to share power with!'

sentences.zh: 」乃召系曰：「汝能行此乎？

translations.literal: She then summoned Xi and said: 'Can you carry this out?'
translations.idiomatic: She called in Xi and asked, 'Can you do this?'

sentences.zh: 」系許諾。

translations.literal: Xi promised assent.
translations.idiomatic: Xi agreed.'

sentences.zh: 即遣內謁者監段恒俊選材勇宦者二百人，授甲長生殿，以帝命召太子。

translations.literal: Immediately she dispatched the inner attendant supervisor Duan Hengjun to select two hundred stalwart eunuchs, arm them in the Hall of Eternal Life, and summon the crown prince by the emperor's order.
translations.idiomatic: At once she sent the inner attendant supervisor Duan Hengjun to choose two hundred brave eunuchs, issue them armor in the Hall of Eternal Life, and summon the crown prince in the emperor's name.

sentences.zh: 元振以告輔國，乃相與勒兵淩霄門，迎太子，以難告。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen informed Fuguo; together they mustered troops at Lingxiao Gate, received the crown prince, and reported the crisis.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen warned Fuguo. Together they rallied troops at Lingxiao Gate, received the crown prince, and told him of the danger.

sentences.zh: 太子曰：「上疾亟，吾可懼死不赴乎？

translations.literal: The crown prince said: 'The sovereign is critically ill—can I, fearing death, refuse to go?'
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince said, 'Father is deathly ill. Am I to fear for my life and refuse to go?'

sentences.zh: 」元振曰：「赴則及禍。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen said: 'If you go, you will meet catastrophe.'
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen said, 'Go—and you walk into disaster.'

sentences.zh: 」乃以兵護太子止飛龍廄，勒兵夜入三殿，收系及恒俊等百余人系之，幽後別殿。

translations.literal: They therefore used troops to keep the crown prince at the Flying Dragon Stables, entered the three halls by night with drawn swords, seized Xi and Hengjun along with more than a hundred others and bound them, and confined the empress in a separate hall.
translations.idiomatic: They held the crown prince at the Flying Dragon Stables under armed guard, then marched by night into the three inner halls, seized Xi, Hengjun, and more than a hundred others, and bound them. The empress they confined in a separate palace.

sentences.zh: 後及系皆為輔國所害。

translations.literal: The empress and Xi were both killed by Fuguo.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguo had both the empress and Xi put to death.

sentences.zh: 系三子：建王武威郡，逌興道，逾齊國公。

translations.literal: Xi had three sons: the Prince of Jian enfeoffed at Wuwei commandery, You Xingdao, and Yu made Duke of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Xi left three sons: the Prince of Jian, enfeoffed at Wuwei; You Xingdao; and Yu, enfeoffed as Duke of Qi.

sentences.zh: 承天皇帝倓，始王建寧。

translations.literal: The Emperor Chengtian Tan was initially Prince of Jianning.
translations.idiomatic: Tan, posthumously honored as Emperor Chengtian, was first enfeoffed as Prince of Jianning.

sentences.zh: 英毅有才略。

translations.literal: Stern and resolute, he possessed talent and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: He was fierce, resolute, and gifted with talent and stratagem.

sentences.zh: 善騎射。

translations.literal: Skilled at mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at horsemanship and archery.

sentences.zh: 祿山亂，典親兵，扈車駕。

translations.literal: When the Lushan rebellion broke out, he commanded the imperial guard and escorted the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rose in rebellion, Tan took command of the imperial guard and escorted the fleeing court.

sentences.zh: 度渭，百姓遮道留太子，太子使喻曰：「至尊播遷，吾可以違左右乎？
