translations.literal: Having crossed the Wei, the common people blocked the road urging the crown prince to stay. The crown prince sent someone to explain: 'The Supreme Sovereign is driven into exile—how can I leave his side?'
translations.idiomatic: After they crossed the Wei River, the people blocked the road and begged the crown prince to remain. The crown prince sent word, 'The Son of Heaven has been driven into exile. How can I leave his side?'

sentences.zh: 」倓進說曰：「逆胡亂常，四海崩分，不因人情圖興復，雖欲從上入蜀，而散關以東非國家有。

translations.literal: Tan advanced to counsel: 'The rebellious barbarian has upset the order; the four seas split apart. If we do not rally human sentiment to plan restoration, even if we wish to follow the sovereign into Shu, east of San Pass will no longer belong to the state.'
translations.idiomatic: Tan pressed forward and said, 'This rebel has overturned the realm and shattered the empire. If we do not seize the people's will and plan restoration, then even if we follow the emperor into Shu, everything east of San Pass will be lost to the dynasty.'

sentences.zh: 夫大孝莫若安社稷，殿下當募豪桀，趣河西，收牧馬。

translations.literal: The greatest filial piety is to secure the altars of state. Your Highness should recruit bold heroes, hasten to Hexi, and gather the horse herds.
translations.idiomatic: The highest filial duty is to secure the altars of state. Your Highness should recruit bold men, march swiftly into Hexi, and gather the frontier horse herds.

sentences.zh: 今防邊屯士不下十萬，而光弼、子儀全軍在河朔，與謀興復，策之上者。

translations.literal: The border garrison troops today number no fewer than a hundred thousand, while Guangbi and Ziyi's full armies stand in Hebei—joining them to plan restoration is the finest strategy.'
translations.idiomatic: The frontier garrisons field no fewer than a hundred thousand men, and Guangbi and Ziyi still hold their full strength in Hebei. Unite with them to plan restoration—that is the supreme course.'

sentences.zh: 」廣平王亦贊之，於是議定。

translations.literal: The Prince of Guangping also endorsed this, and so the plan was settled.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Guangping agreed as well, and the decision was made.

sentences.zh: 太子北過渭，兵仗鹽惡，士氣崩沮，日數十戰。

translations.literal: As the crown prince proceeded north across the Wei, weapons and provisions were poor, morale collapsed, and they fought dozens of battles daily.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince pushed north beyond the Wei with wretched arms and rations. Morale crumbled. Day after day they fought battle upon battle.

sentences.zh: 倓以驍騎數百從，每接戰，常身先，血殷袂，不告也。

translations.literal: Tan followed with several hundred crack cavalry; in every engagement he rode at the fore, his sleeves dyed red with blood, and never spoke of it.
translations.idiomatic: Tan rode behind with several hundred elite horsemen. In every clash he charged at the front, his sleeves soaked dark with blood—and never once complained of it.

sentences.zh: 太子或過時未食，倓輒涕泗不自勝，三軍皆屬目。

translations.literal: When the crown prince sometimes went without food for hours, Tan would weep uncontrollably—the whole army took notice.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince went hungry past the hour of his meal, Tan wept until he could not speak for grief. All three armies looked on.

sentences.zh: 至靈武，太子即帝位，議以倓為天下兵馬元帥，左右固請廣平王。

translations.literal: Upon reaching Lingwu, the crown prince ascended the throne. They debated making Tan Grand Marshal of All Armies, but his attendants firmly pressed for the Prince of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: At Lingwu the crown prince took the throne. The court considered making Tan supreme commander of all armies, but his attendants pressed hard for the Prince of Guangping instead.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「廣平既冢嗣，安用元帥？

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'Guangping is already heir apparent—why need a grand marshal?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, 'Guangping is already heir apparent. Why make him a field marshal?'

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「太子從曰撫軍，守曰監國。

translations.literal: They replied: 'When the crown prince takes the field it is called pacifying the armies; when he holds the fort it is overseeing the state.'
translations.idiomatic: They answered, 'When the crown prince leads an army, he is said to pacify the host; when he holds the capital, he oversees the realm.'

sentences.zh: 元帥，撫軍也，莫宜於廣平王。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal is the pacifier of armies—none suits the Prince of Guangping better.'
translations.idiomatic: Field marshal means pacifier of armies—and no one is more fitting than the Prince of Guangping.'

sentences.zh: 」帝從之，更詔倓典親軍，以李輔國為府司馬。

translations.literal: The emperor assented. A new edict put Tan in charge of the imperial guard, with Li Fuguo as army adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed. A new order placed Tan in command of the imperial guard, with Li Fuguo as his adjutant.

sentences.zh: 時張良娣有寵，與輔國交構，欲以動皇嗣者。

translations.literal: At that time Lady Zhang Liangdi enjoyed favor and colluded with Fuguo, intending to move against the heir.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Lady Zhang Liangdi held the emperor's favor and plotted with Fuguo to undermine the succession.

sentences.zh: 倓忠謇，數為帝言之，由是為良娣、輔國所譖，妄曰：「倓恨不總兵，郁郁有異志。

translations.literal: Tan was loyal and outspoken, repeatedly reporting this to the emperor; for this he was slandered by Lady Zhang and Fuguo, who falsely said: 'Tan resents not commanding the armies and broods with rebellious intent.'
translations.idiomatic: Tan was upright and blunt, and repeatedly warned the emperor. Lady Zhang and Fuguo therefore slandered him, claiming, 'Tan resents being denied command of the armies and broods with treason in his heart.'

sentences.zh: 」帝惑偏語，賜倓死，俄悔悟。

translations.literal: The emperor, swayed by partisan words, ordered Tan to take his own life. Soon after he came to his senses with regret.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, misled by their private whispers, ordered Tan to die. Before long he awoke to what he had done—and grieved.

sentences.zh: 明年，廣平王收二京，使李泌獻捷。

translations.literal: The following year, the Prince of Guangping recovered the two capitals and sent Li Bi to present the victory report.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Prince of Guangping retook the two capitals and sent Li Bi to bear the news of victory.

sentences.zh: 泌與帝雅素，從容語倓事，帝改容曰：「倓於艱難時實自有力，為細人間鬩，欲害其兄，我計社稷，割愛而為之所。

translations.literal: Bi was on long-standing familiar terms with the emperor. Speaking at ease of Tan's affair, the emperor changed expression and said: 'Tan truly exerted himself in those hard times. Petty men stirred discord, seeking to harm his elder brother—I weighed the altars of state and cut my own flesh to act for them.'
translations.idiomatic: Bi had long been close to the emperor. As they spoke easily of Tan's case, the emperor's face changed. He said, 'In those bitter days Tan truly did his part. Small men set brother against brother, and I weighed the realm against my own flesh—and cut what I loved most to preserve the throne.'

sentences.zh: 」泌曰：「爾時臣在河西，知其詳。

translations.literal: Bi said: 'At that time I was in Hexi and knew the details.'
translations.idiomatic: Bi said, 'I was in Hexi then and knew the truth.'

sentences.zh: 廣平於兄弟篤睦，至今言建寧，則嗚咽不自己。

translations.literal: The Prince of Guangping is deeply affectionate toward his brothers—even now, speaking of Jianning, he sobs beyond control.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Guangping loves his brothers dearly. Even now, at the name of Jianning, he weeps until he cannot stop.

sentences.zh: 陛下此言得之讒口耳。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's words come from slanderers' mouths alone.'
translations.idiomatic: What Your Majesty has heard came from poison tongues alone.'

sentences.zh: 」帝泣下曰：「事已爾，末耐何！

translations.literal: The emperor wept and said: 'The deed is done—what can be borne of it!'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept and said, 'It is done already. What can be undone now?'

sentences.zh: 」泌曰：「陛下嘗聞《黃臺瓜》乎？

translations.literal: Bi said: 'Has Your Majesty ever heard of the Melons on the Yellow Platform?'
translations.idiomatic: Bi said, 'Has Your Majesty ever heard of the Melons on the Yellow Platform?'

sentences.zh: 高宗有八子，天後所生者四人，自為行，而睿宗最幼。

translations.literal: Gaozong had eight sons. Four were born to Empress Tian—they ranked themselves by birth order, and Ruizong was the youngest.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong had eight sons. The Empress Wu bore four of them. Among themselves they ordered their ranks by age, and Ruizong was the youngest.

sentences.zh: 長曰弘，為太子，仁明孝友，後方圖臨朝，鴆鐐之，而立次子賢。

translations.literal: The eldest, Hong, was crown prince—benevolent, clear-minded, filial and fraternal. When the empress later plotted to hold court herself, she poisoned him and installed the second son Xian as heir.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest was Hong, made crown prince—humane, bright, filial, and devoted to his brothers. When the empress later schemed to rule in her own name, she poisoned him and set up the second son, Xian, as heir.

sentences.zh: 賢日憂惕，每侍上，不敢有言，乃作樂章，使工歌之，欲以感悟上及後。

translations.literal: Xian lived each day in anxious dread. Whenever he attended the emperor he dared not speak openly; instead he composed a lyric and had musicians sing it, hoping to move the emperor and the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Xian lived in daily fear. Whenever he attended his father he dared not speak plainly. Instead he wrote a song and had musicians perform it, hoping to move the emperor and the empress alike.

sentences.zh: 其言曰：『種瓜黃臺下，瓜熟子離離。

translations.literal: Its words ran: 'Melons planted below the Yellow Platform—when ripe, the fruit hangs thick.'
translations.idiomatic: The words ran, 'Melons planted below the Yellow Platform—when ripe, the fruit hangs heavy.'

sentences.zh: 一摘使瓜好，再摘令瓜稀。

translations.literal: One plucking leaves the melons fair; a second thins the vine.
translations.idiomatic: One picking and the melons grow fine; a second picking and the vine grows sparse.

sentences.zh: 三摘尚雲可，四摘抱蔓歸。

translations.literal: A third plucking—and still one may say enough; a fourth plucking leaves only the bare stem clinging to the vine.'
translations.idiomatic: A third picking—and one may still say it will do; a fourth picking, and only the bare stem remains on the vine.'

sentences.zh: 』而賢終為後所斥，死黔中。

translations.literal: Yet Xian was ultimately cast out by the empress and died in Qianzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the end Xian was cast out by the empress and died in exile at Qianzhong.

sentences.zh: 陛下今一摘矣，慎無再！

translations.literal: Your Majesty has already plucked once—take care not to pluck again!'
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has already plucked once—take care not to pluck again!'

sentences.zh: 」帝愕然曰：「公安得是言？

translations.literal: The emperor started and said: 'How can you, sir, speak such words?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor started and said, 'How can you, sir, speak such words?'

sentences.zh: 」是時，廣平有大功，亦為後所構，故泌因對及之，廣平遂安。

translations.literal: At that time Guangping had great merit and was also framed by the empress; therefore Bi spoke to this point in his reply, and Guangping was thereby secured.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Prince of Guangping had won great merit and was also framed by the empress; Bi therefore raised the matter in his reply, and Guangping was secured.

sentences.zh: 及即位，追贈倓齊王。

translations.literal: When he took the throne, Tan was posthumously made Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: When Daizong took the throne, Tan was posthumously created Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 大歷三年，有詔以倓當艱難時，首定大謀，排眾議，於中興有功，乃進謚承天皇帝，以興信公主季女張為恭順皇后，冥配焉，葬順陵，祔主奉天皇帝廟，同殿異室雲。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dali an edict said that Tan, in hard times, first settled the great plan, overrode the multitude's counsel, and had merit in the restoration; he was therefore advanced in posthumous title to Emperor Chengtian, with the youngest daughter Zhang of the Princess of Xingxin made Empress Gongshun for a posthumous marriage; he was buried at Shun Mausoleum and his spirit tablet placed in the temple of Emperor Fengtian, in the same hall but a separate chamber.
translations.idiomatic: In 768 an edict declared that Tan, in the darkest days, had first settled the great design, overrode dissent, and served the restoration—he was posthumously elevated as Emperor Chengtian. The youngest daughter Zhang of the Princess of Xingxin was made Empress Gongshun for a posthumous marriage. He was buried at Shun Mausoleum, with his spirit tablet in the temple of Emperor Fengtian, in the same hall but a separate chamber.

sentences.zh: 初，李泌請加贈倓，代宗曰：「倓性忠孝，而困於讒，追帝之，若何？

translations.literal: At first Li Bi requested additional honors for Tan. Daizong said: 'Tan was loyal and filial yet trapped by slander—if we posthumously make him emperor, what then?'
translations.idiomatic: At first Li Bi asked that Tan receive further honors. Daizong said, 'Tan was loyal and filial yet trapped by slander—if we posthumously make him emperor, what then?'

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「開元中，上皇兄弟皆贈太子。

translations.literal: The reply was: 'In the Kaiyuan period the Retired Emperor's brothers were all posthumously made crown princes.'
translations.idiomatic: The reply was, 'In the Kaiyuan period the Retired Emperor's brothers were all posthumously made crown princes.'

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「是特祖宗友愛耳，豈若倓有功乎？

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'That was merely the ancestral family's affection—how can it compare with Tan's merit?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, 'That was merely the ancestral family's affection—how can it compare with Tan's merit?'

sentences.zh: 」於是追帝號。

translations.literal: Thereupon the posthumous imperial title was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the posthumous imperial title was granted.

sentences.zh: 遣使迎喪彭原，既至城門，喪輴不動。

translations.literal: Envoys were sent to welcome the coffin from Pengyuan; when it reached the city gate the funeral carriage would not move.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys were sent to welcome the coffin from Pengyuan. When it reached the city gate the funeral carriage would not move.

sentences.zh: 帝謂泌曰：「豈有恨邪？

translations.literal: The emperor said to Bi: 'Is there resentment?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Bi, 'Is there resentment?'

sentences.zh: 卿往祭之，以白朕意。

translations.literal: Go and offer sacrifice, and make my intent known.
translations.idiomatic: Go and offer sacrifice, and make my intent known.

sentences.zh: 且卿及知倓艱難定策者。

translations.literal: And you, together with those who knew Tan's hardships and settled the plan.'
translations.idiomatic: And you, together with those who knew Tan's hardships and settled the plan.'

sentences.zh: 」泌為挽詞二解，追述倓誌，命挽士唱，泌因進輴，乃行，觀者皆為垂泣。

translations.literal: Bi composed two elegiac stanzas recounting Tan's intent, ordered the pallbearers to sing them, and advanced the carriage—it then moved, and all who watched wept.
translations.idiomatic: Bi composed two elegiac stanzas recounting Tan's intent, ordered the pallbearers to sing them, and advanced the carriage—it then moved, and all who watched wept.

sentences.zh: 彭王亻堇，始王新城，進封彭。

translations.literal: Prince Peng Jin was first Prince of Xincheng, then advanced to Prince of Peng.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Peng Jin was first Prince of Xincheng, then advanced to Prince of Peng.

sentences.zh: 史思明陷河、洛，人心震騷，群臣請以諸王臨統方鎮兵，遙相維壓。

translations.literal: When Shi Siming took He and Luo, hearts trembled; the ministers requested that the princes personally command the regional armies to exert mutual pressure from afar.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Siming took the He and Luo region, the people were shaken. Ministers asked that the princes personally command the regional armies to exert mutual pressure from afar.

sentences.zh: 於是詔亻堇充河西節度，兗王北庭，涇王隴右，杞王陜西，興王鳳翔，並為大使。

translations.literal: An edict thereupon made Jin commissioner of Hexi, the Prince of Yan of Beiting, the Prince of Jing of Longyou, the Prince of Qi of Shaanxi, and the Prince of Xing of Fengxiang—all as grand commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: An edict thereupon made Jin commissioner of Hexi; the Prince of Yan, of Beiting; the Prince of Jing, of Longyou; the Prince of Qi, of Shaanxi; and the Prince of Xing, of Fengxiang—all as grand commissioners.

sentences.zh: 是歲亻堇薨。

translations.literal: That year Jin died.
translations.idiomatic: That year Jin died.

sentences.zh: 子鎮為常山郡王。

translations.literal: His son Zhen was made Prince of Changshan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhen was created Prince of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 兗王亻閑，始王潁川，進王兗。

translations.literal: Prince Yan Xian was first Prince of Yingchuan, then advanced to Prince of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yan Xian was first Prince of Yingchuan, then advanced to Prince of Yan.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Baoying.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 762.

sentences.zh: 涇王侹，始王東陽，進王涇。

translations.literal: Prince Jing Ting was first Prince of Dongyang, then advanced to Prince of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jing Ting was first Prince of Dongyang, then advanced to Prince of Jing.

sentences.zh: 興元元年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 784.

sentences.zh: 鄆王榮，始王靈昌。

translations.literal: Prince Yun Rong was first Prince of Lingchang.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yun Rong was first Prince of Lingchang.

sentences.zh: 蚤薨，追封。

translations.literal: He died young; posthumous enfeoffment was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He died young; posthumous enfeoffment was granted.

sentences.zh: 襄王僙，至德二載始王，與杞、召、興、定四王同封。

translations.literal: Prince Xiang Qian was first enfeoffed in the second year of Zhide, together with the Princes of Qi, Shao, Xing, and Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiang Qian was first enfeoffed in 757, together with the Princes of Qi, Shao, Xing, and Ding.

sentences.zh: 貞元七年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the seventh year of Zhenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 791.

sentences.zh: 子宣為伊吾郡王，寀樂安王。

translations.literal: His sons Xuan was Prince of Yiwu commandery and Cai Prince of Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Xuan was Prince of Yiwu and Cai Prince of Le'an.

sentences.zh: 宣裔孫煴。

translations.literal: Xuan's descendant was Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's descendant was Yun.

sentences.zh: 煴，性謹柔，材無過人者。

translations.literal: Yun was cautious and gentle by nature, his talent no better than ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was cautious and gentle by nature, his talent no better than ordinary.

sentences.zh: 光啟二年，田令孜逼僖宗幸興元，邠寧節度使硃玫以五千騎追乘輿不及。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangqi, Tian Lingze forced Emperor Xizong to go to Xingyuan; Zhu Mei, military governor of Binning, pursued with five thousand horsemen but could not overtake the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: In 886 Tian Lingze forced Emperor Xizong to flee to Xingyuan. Zhu Mei, military governor of Binning, pursued with five thousand horsemen but could not overtake the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 煴以疾不能從，玫劫之，駐鳳翔，得臺省官百余，乃脅宰相蕭遘等率群臣盟石鼻驛，奉煴為嗣襄王，監軍國事，因還京師，即封拜官屬。

translations.literal: Yun, ill, could not follow; Mei seized him, halted at Fengxiang, gathered more than a hundred court officials, and coerced Chancellor Xiao Gou and others to lead the ministers in oath at Shibi Post, installing Yun as heir to the Prince of Xiang to oversee state affairs; they then returned to the capital and immediately enfeoffed and appointed his staff.
translations.idiomatic: Yun, too ill to follow, was seized by Mei, who halted at Fengxiang, gathered more than a hundred court officials, and coerced Chancellor Xiao Gou and others to lead the ministers in oath at Shibi Post, installing Yun as heir to the Prince of Xiang to oversee state affairs. They then returned to the capital and immediately enfeoffed and appointed his staff.

sentences.zh: 初，遘執不可，於是罷遘，而玫自為侍中，號令己出。

translations.literal: At first Gou firmly refused; he was therefore dismissed, while Mei made himself chief minister and issued orders as he pleased.
translations.idiomatic: At first Gou firmly refused; he was therefore dismissed, while Mei made himself chief minister and issued orders as he pleased.

sentences.zh: 以裴澈為門下侍郎，鄭昌圖中書侍郎，皆平章事。

translations.literal: Pei Che was made vice director of the Secretariat and Zheng Changtu vice director of the Chancellery—both grand councilors.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Che was made vice director of the Secretariat and Zheng Changtu vice director of the Chancellery—both grand councilors.

sentences.zh: 遣柳陟等十余人分諭天下嗣襄王所以監國意，皆得進官。

translations.literal: Liu Zhi and more than ten others were sent to announce throughout the realm the heir's intent to oversee state affairs; all received advancement in office.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhi and more than ten others were sent to announce throughout the realm the heir's intent to oversee state affairs; all received advancement in office.

sentences.zh: 玫又脅太子太師裴璩等奉箋勸進，煴五讓乃即位，改元建貞，尊僖宗為太上元皇聖帝。

translations.literal: Mei also coerced Grand Tutor Pei Zhen and others to submit a memorial urging accession; Yun declined five times before taking the throne, changed the era name to Jianzhen, and honored Xizong as Supreme Primordial Sacred Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Mei also coerced Grand Tutor Pei Zhen and others to submit a memorial urging accession. Yun declined five times before taking the throne, changed the era name to Jianzhen, and honored Xizong as Supreme Primordial Sacred Emperor.

sentences.zh: 河中節度使王重榮率諸籓貢奉，歸者十八九，而蔡州秦宗權自僭號，惟太原李克用不從。

translations.literal: Wang Chongrong, military governor of Hezhong, led the various circuits in tribute; eight or nine in ten submitted, while Qin Zongquan of Caizhou arrogated imperial title—only Li Keyong of Taiyuan did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chongrong, military governor of Hezhong, led the various circuits in tribute; eight or nine in ten submitted, while Qin Zongquan of Caizhou arrogated imperial title—only Li Keyong of Taiyuan did not follow.

sentences.zh: 時帝遣使喻重榮、克用，故二人聽命。

translations.literal: The emperor then sent envoys to persuade Chongrong and Keyong; the two therefore obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then sent envoys to persuade Chongrong and Keyong; the two therefore obeyed.

sentences.zh: 樞密使楊復恭等傳檄三輔，募能斬玫者，以邠寧節度界之。

translations.literal: Yang Fugong, commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and others circulated proclamations in the three capital districts, recruiting anyone who could kill Mei, promising the Binning command in reward.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fugong, commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and others circulated proclamations in the three capital districts, recruiting anyone who could kill Mei, promising the Binning command in reward.

sentences.zh: 其偽將王行瑜自鳳州入京師殺玫，而煴與澈、昌圖並官屬奔東渭橋。

translations.literal: Mei's false general Wang Xingyu entered the capital from Fengzhou and killed Mei; Yun fled with Che, Changtu, and the entire staff to the Eastern Wei Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Mei's false general Wang Xingyu entered the capital from Fengzhou and killed Mei. Yun fled with Che, Changtu, and the entire staff to the Eastern Wei Bridge.

sentences.zh: 重榮紿使迎之，煴與官屬別，且泣曰：「朕見重榮，當令備所服迓公等。

translations.literal: Chongrong deceived them into coming to meet him; Yun parted from his staff and wept: 'When I see Chongrong I shall have your proper robes prepared to welcome you.'
translations.idiomatic: Chongrong deceived them into coming to meet him. Yun parted from his staff and wept, 'When I see Chongrong I shall have your proper robes prepared to welcome you.'

sentences.zh: 」至蒲，執殺之，因械澈等於獄，誅殺偽官，函煴首至行在所。

translations.literal: At Pu he was seized and killed; Che and the others were shackled in prison, false officials were executed, and Yun's head was sent in a box to the emperor's camp.
translations.idiomatic: At Pu he was seized and killed. Che and the others were shackled in prison, false officials were executed, and Yun's head was sent in a box to the emperor's camp.

sentences.zh: 煴即偽位凡九月敗。

translations.literal: Yun had held the false throne for nine months before defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Yun had held the false throne for nine months before defeat.

sentences.zh: 始，煴首至，群臣白帝禦興元南門受之，百官稱賀。

translations.literal: When Yun's head first arrived, the ministers reported that the emperor should receive it at the southern gate of Xingyuan; the officials congratulated him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yun's head first arrived, the ministers reported that the emperor should receive it at the southern gate of Xingyuan; the officials congratulated him.

sentences.zh: 太常博士殷盈孫奏言：「禮，公族有罪，有司曰：『某之罪在大辟。

translations.literal: Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Yin Yingsun memorialized: 'By ritual, when a member of the ducal clan is guilty, the relevant office says: So-and-so's crime warrants capital punishment.'
translations.idiomatic: Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Yin Yingsun memorialized, 'By ritual, when a member of the ducal clan is guilty, the relevant office says, So-and-so's crime warrants capital punishment.'

sentences.zh: 』君曰：『赦之。

translations.literal: The ruler says: 'Pardon him.'
translations.idiomatic: The ruler says, Pardon him.'

sentences.zh: 』如是者三，走出，致刑焉，君為素服不舉者三日。

translations.literal: This is done three times; the guilty one goes out and punishment is carried out; the ruler wears plain dress and abstains from music for three days.
translations.idiomatic: This is done three times; the guilty one goes out and punishment is carried out; the ruler wears plain dress and abstains from music for three days.

sentences.zh: 今煴皇族，以不能固節，迫脅至此，宜廢為庶人，絕屬籍，葬以庶人禮。

translations.literal: Now Yun is of the imperial clan; because he could not hold firm to integrity and was coerced to this point, he should be deposed to commoner status, cut from the genealogy, and buried with commoner's rites.
translations.idiomatic: Now Yun is of the imperial clan; because he could not hold firm to integrity and was coerced to this point, he should be deposed to commoner status, cut from the genealogy, and buried with commoner's rites.

sentences.zh: 大捷之慶，須硃玫首至乃賀。

translations.literal: The celebration of great victory should wait until Zhu Mei's head arrives.
translations.idiomatic: The celebration of great victory should wait until Zhu Mei's head arrives.'

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: The edict granted approval.
translations.idiomatic: The edict granted approval.

sentences.zh: 杞王倕，貞元十四年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Qi Chun died in the fourteenth year of Zhenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Qi Chun died in 798.

sentences.zh: 召王偲，元和元年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Shao Si died in the first year of Yuanhe.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shao Si died in 806.

sentences.zh: 恭懿太子佋，始封興王。

translations.literal: Posthumous Crown Prince Gongyi Zhao was first enfeoffed as Prince of Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao, posthumously styled Crown Prince Gongyi, was first created Prince of Xing.

sentences.zh: 上元元年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Shangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 760.

sentences.zh: 佋生，後方專愛，帝最憐之。

translations.literal: When Zhao was born, the empress held exclusive favor, and the emperor doted on him most.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao was born, the empress already monopolized the emperor's affection, and of all his children the emperor cherished this boy above the rest.

sentences.zh: 後數撼儲嫡，欲以佋嗣，會薨，計塞。

translations.literal: The empress repeatedly undermined the heir apparent, intending to install Zhao as successor; but he died, and the plan came to nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Again and again the empress assailed the legitimate heir, scheming to put Zhao in his place—but the boy died, and her design collapsed.

sentences.zh: 是夕，帝及後夢佋辭決流涕去，帝鯁悵，故冊贈皇太子。

translations.literal: That very night the emperor and empress dreamed of Zhao taking leave in tears; the emperor was stricken with grief, and therefore posthumously created him crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: That same night the emperor and empress dreamed of Zhao bidding them farewell in tears. Stricken with grief, the emperor posthumously created him crown prince.

sentences.zh: 定王侗，寶應初薨。

translations.literal: Prince Ding Tong died at the beginning of the Baoying era.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ding Tong died in the early Baoying era (c. 762–763).

sentences.zh: 代宗二十子：睿真皇后生德宗皇帝，崔妃生邈，貞懿皇后生迥；

translations.literal: Daizong had twenty sons: Empress Ruizhen bore the future Emperor Dezong; Consort Cui bore Yao; Empress Zhenyi bore Jiong;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daizong had twenty sons. Empress Ruizhen bore the future Emperor Dezong; Consort Cui bore Yao; Empress Zhenyi bore Jiong;

sentences.zh: 十七王，史亡其母之氏、位。

translations.literal: As for the other seventeen princes, the histories do not record their mothers' clans or titles.
translations.idiomatic: Of the remaining seventeen princes, the histories have lost record of their mothers' clans and ranks.

sentences.zh: 昭靖太子邈，好學，以賢聞。

translations.literal: Posthumous Crown Prince Zhaojing Yao was fond of learning and renowned for virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Yao, posthumously styled Crown Prince Zhaojing, loved study and was known throughout the court for his excellence.

sentences.zh: 上元二年始王益昌。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shangyuan he was first enfeoffed as Prince of Yichang.
translations.idiomatic: In 761 he was first created Prince of Yichang.

sentences.zh: 帝即位，寶應元年進王鄭，與韓王同封。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne, in the first year of Baoying he was advanced to Prince of Zheng and enfeoffed together with the Prince of Han.
translations.idiomatic: When Daizong ascended the throne, Yao was promoted to Prince of Zheng in 762 and enfeoffed on the same day as the Prince of Han.

sentences.zh: 淄青牙將李懷玉逐其帥侯希逸，詔邈為平盧淄青節度大使，以懷玉知留後。

translations.literal: When the Ya-jiang Li Huaiyu of Ziqing drove out his commander Hou Xiyi, an edict made Yao grand commissioner of Pinglu-Ziqing, with Huaiyu serving as acting commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Huaiyu, a junior officer of the Ziqing garrison, expelled his commander Hou Xiyi, the court appointed Yao grand commissioner of Pinglu-Ziqing and made Huaiyu acting commander.

sentences.zh: 大歷初，代皇太子為天下兵馬元帥。

translations.literal: In the early Dali era he replaced the crown prince as overall commander of armies under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Dali era (c. 766) he replaced the crown prince as commander-in-chief of all imperial forces.

sentences.zh: 八年薨，遂罷元帥府。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he died, and the marshal's headquarters was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 773, and the marshal's headquarters was dissolved.

sentences.zh: 均王遐，早薨。

translations.literal: Prince Jun Xia died young.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jun Xia died in infancy.

sentences.zh: 貞元八年追封。

translations.literal: Posthumous enfeoffment was granted in the eighth year of Zhenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed in 792.

sentences.zh: 睦王述。

translations.literal: Prince Mu Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Mu Shu.

sentences.zh: 大歷十年，田承嗣不臣，而昭靖夭，無強王，帝乃悉王諸子，領諸鎮軍，威天下。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Dali, Tian Chengsi proved disloyal, and Zhaojing died young; with no prince of standing, the emperor enfeoffed all his sons and placed them over the garrisons of the various circuits to awe the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In 775, Tian Chengsi turned rebel and Yao died prematurely. Lacking a prince of stature, the emperor enfeoffed every one of his sons and set them over the military circuits to overawe the empire.

sentences.zh: 於是以述為睦王，領嶺南節度，逾郴王、渭北鄜坊節度，過韓王、汴宋節度，造忻王、昭義節度，皆為大使；

translations.literal: Shu was made Prince of Mu and given the Lingnan governorship; Yu became Prince of Chen and took Weibei Bianfang; Guo became Prince of Han and took Biansong; Zao became Prince of Xin and took Zhaoyi—all as grand commissioners;
translations.idiomatic: Shu was created Prince of Mu and made grand commissioner of Lingnan; Yu, Prince of Chen, of Weibei Bianfang; Guo, Prince of Han, of Biansong; and Zao, Prince of Xin, of Zhaoyi.

sentences.zh: 連為恩王，遘鄜王，暹韶王，遇端王，遹循王，通恭王，逵原王，逸雅王，並開府儀同三司，然不出閤。

translations.literal: Lian was Prince of En; Gou, Prince of Zou; Xian, Prince of Shao; Yu, Prince of Duan; Yuan, Prince of Xun; Tong, Prince of Gong; Kui, Prince of Yuan; and Yi, Prince of Ya—all received the title of Grand Preceptor of the State, Third Rank, yet none left the palace confines.
translations.idiomatic: Lian became Prince of En; Gou, Prince of Zou; Xian, Prince of Shao; Yu, Prince of Duan; Yuan, Prince of Xun; Tong, Prince of Gong; Kui, Prince of Yuan; and Yi, Prince of Ya. All were granted the title of Grand Preceptor of the State, Third Rank, yet none ever left the palace.

sentences.zh: 德宗建中初，周天下訪太后所在，述於諸王最長，故拜奉迎太后使，以工部尚書喬琳副之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianzhong era under Dezong, the court searched the realm for the empress dowager's whereabouts; Shu was eldest among the princes, so he was appointed commissioner to welcome her back, with Vice Minister of Works Qiao Lin as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jianzhong era, Emperor Dezong ordered a search across the empire for the empress dowager. Shu was the eldest prince, and so was appointed commissioner to escort her home, with Vice Minister of Works Qiao Lin as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 貞元七年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the seventh year of Zhenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 791.

sentences.zh: 丹王逾，始王郴，建中四年，與簡王同徙封。

translations.literal: Prince Dan Yu was first Prince of Chen; in the fourth year of Jianzhong he was transferred in title together with the Prince of Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Dan Yu was first Prince of Chen; in 783 he and the Prince of Jian had their fiefs changed.

sentences.zh: 元和十五年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the fifteenth year of Yuanhe.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 820.

sentences.zh: 恩王連，元和十二年薨。

translations.literal: Prince En Lian died in the twelfth year of Yuanhe.
translations.idiomatic: Prince En Lian died in 817.

sentences.zh: 韓王迥，始王延慶郡，以母寵，故與鄭王先徙封。

translations.literal: Prince Han Jiong was first Prince of Yanqing commandery; because his mother enjoyed favor, he and the Prince of Zheng were the first to have their fiefs changed.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Han Jiong was first Prince of Yanqing; favored because of his mother's standing, he and the Prince of Zheng were the first to receive new fiefs.

sentences.zh: 貞元十二年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the twelfth year of Zhenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 796.

sentences.zh: 簡王遘，始王鄜，徙封簡。

translations.literal: Prince Jian Gou was first Prince of Zou; his fief was changed to Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jian Gou was first Prince of Zou, then transferred to Prince of Jian.

sentences.zh: 元和四年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the fourth year of Yuanhe.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 809.

sentences.zh: 益王乃，大歷十四年始王。

translations.literal: Prince Yi Nai was first enfeoffed in the fourteenth year of Dali.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yi Nai was first enfeoffed in 779.

sentences.zh: 亡薨年。

translations.literal: The year of death is unrecorded.
translations.idiomatic: The year of his death is unrecorded.

sentences.zh: 隋王迅，興元元年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Sui Xun died in the first year of Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Sui Xun died in 784.

sentences.zh: 荊王選，蚤薨，建中二年追王。

translations.literal: Prince Jing Xuan died young; in the second year of Jianzhong he was posthumously enfeoffed as prince.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jing Xuan died in infancy; in 781 he was posthumously created a prince.

sentences.zh: 蜀王溯，本名遂，大歷十四年始王，建中二年改今名。

translations.literal: Prince Shu Su—originally named Sui—was first enfeoffed in the fourteenth year of Dali; in the second year of Jianzhong his present name was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shu Su, originally named Sui, was first enfeoffed in 779; in 781 he took his present name.

sentences.zh: 忻王造，元和六年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Xin Zao died in the sixth year of Yuanhe.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xin Zao died in 811.

sentences.zh: 韶王暹，貞元十二年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Shao Xian died in the twelfth year of Zhenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shao Xian died in 796.

sentences.zh: 嘉王運，貞元十七年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Jia Yun died in the seventeenth year of Zhenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jia Yun died in 801.

sentences.zh: 端王遇，貞元七年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Duan Yu died in the seventh year of Zhenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Duan Yu died in 791.

sentences.zh: 循王遹，亡薨年。

translations.literal: Prince Xun Yuan: the year of death is unrecorded.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xun Yuan: the year of his death is unrecorded.

sentences.zh: 恭王通，亡薨年。

translations.literal: Prince Gong Tong: the year of death is unrecorded.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Gong Tong: the year of his death is unrecorded.

sentences.zh: 原王逵，大和六年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Yuan Kui died in the sixth year of Dahe.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yuan Kui died in 832.

sentences.zh: 雅王逸，貞元十五年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Ya Yi died in the fifteenth year of Zhenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ya Yi died in 799.

sentences.zh: 德宗十一子：昭德皇后生順宗皇帝，帝取昭靖太子子誼為第二子，又取順宗子謜為第六子；

translations.literal: Dezong had eleven sons: Empress Zhaode bore the future Emperor Shunzong; the emperor took Yi, son of Posthumous Crown Prince Zhaojing, as his second son, and also took Yuan, son of Shunzong, as his sixth son;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong had eleven sons. Empress Zhaode bore the future Emperor Shunzong. The emperor adopted Yi, son of the late Crown Prince Zhaojing, as his second son, and Yuan, son of Shunzong, as his sixth.

sentences.zh: 余八王，史亡其母之氏、位。

translations.literal: As for the remaining eight princes, the histories do not record their mothers' clans or titles.
translations.idiomatic: Of the remaining eight princes, the histories have lost record of their mothers' clans and ranks.

sentences.zh: 舒王誼，初名謨。

translations.literal: Prince Shu Yi—originally named Mo.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shu Yi, originally named Mo.

sentences.zh: 帝愛其幼，取為子。

translations.literal: The emperor loved him in his youth and took him as a son.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor doted on the boy in his infancy and took him for his own.

sentences.zh: 大歷十四年始王舒，與通、虔、肅、資四王同封。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Dali he was first enfeoffed as Prince of Shu, together with the Princes Tong, Qian, Su, and Zi.
translations.idiomatic: In 779 he was first created Prince of Shu, enfeoffed on the same occasion as the Princes Tong, Qian, Su, and Zi.

sentences.zh: 拜開府儀同三司，詔有司給奉稍，俄以軍興罷。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Preceptor of the State, Third Rank; an edict ordered the relevant offices to supply his stipend, but soon, with military campaigns under way, this was discontinued.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the title of Grand Preceptor of the State, Third Rank, and the court ordered his maintenance paid from the treasury—but when war broke out, the allowance was soon withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 謨於諸王最長，帝欲試以事，故拜涇原節度大使。

translations.literal: Mo was eldest among the princes; the emperor wished to test him with responsibility, and therefore appointed him grand commissioner of Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Mo was the eldest prince, and the emperor wished to try him in office; he was therefore made grand commissioner of Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 時尚父郭子儀病篤，帝臨軒遣謨持詔往視。

translations.literal: At that time the Grand Preceptor Guo Ziyi was gravely ill; the emperor came to the hall and sent Mo with an edict to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi, the Grand Preceptor, lay gravely ill. The emperor came to the throne hall and dispatched Mo with an edict to inquire after him.

sentences.zh: 謨冠遠遊冠，禦絳袍，乘象輅四馬，飛龍士三百，國府官皆袴褶以從。

translations.literal: Mo wore the traveling crown and a crimson robe, rode a four-horse elephant chariot with three hundred Dragon Flight guards, and all officials of the National Administration followed in short jackets and riding breeches.
translations.idiomatic: Mo wore the far-traveling crown and a crimson robe, rode a four-horse state carriage escorted by three hundred Dragon Flight guards, and every officer of the National Administration followed in riding dress.

sentences.zh: 子儀手叩頭謝恩。

translations.literal: Ziyi bowed with hands joined in gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi pressed his palms together and bowed to the ground in thanks.

sentences.zh: 謨宣詔已，乃易服勞問還。

translations.literal: After Mo had read the edict, he changed dress, paid his respects, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Once the edict had been read, Mo changed out of his ceremonial garb, offered his personal respects, and returned.

sentences.zh: 於是，李希烈反，招討使李勉戰不勝，奔宋州，朝廷大震。

translations.literal: Then Li Xilie rebelled; the punitive commissioner Li Mian fought without success and fled to Song prefecture, and the court was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Then Li Xilie rose in rebellion. The punitive commissioner Li Mian was defeated and fled to Songzhou, and the court was thrown into alarm.

sentences.zh: 乃拜謨揚州大都督、荊襄江西沔鄂節度使、諸軍行營兵馬都元帥。

translations.literal: Mo was thereupon made governor-general of Yangzhou, military commissioner of Jing-Xiang, Jiangxi, Mian, and E, and supreme commander of all expeditionary forces.
translations.idiomatic: Mo was thereupon appointed governor-general of Yangzhou, military commissioner over Jing-Xiang, Jiangxi, Mian, and E, and supreme commander of all expeditionary armies.

sentences.zh: 改名誼。

translations.literal: His name was changed to Yi.
translations.idiomatic: His name was changed to Yi.

sentences.zh: 軍中以哥舒翰由元帥敗，而王所封同之，帝乃使徙王普。

translations.literal: In the army it was said that Geshu Han had been defeated while holding the title of marshal, and the prince's fief bore the same name; the emperor therefore had him transferred to Prince of Pu.
translations.idiomatic: The troops recalled that Geshu Han had met disaster while serving as marshal—and the prince's fief shared that very name. The emperor therefore transferred him to Prince of Pu.

sentences.zh: 以兵部侍郎蕭復為統軍長史，湖南觀察使孔巢父為行軍左司馬，山南東道節度行軍司馬樊澤為右，刑部員外郎劉從一、侍御史韋儹為判官，兵部員外郎高參掌書記，右金吾大將軍渾瑊為中軍虞候，江西節度使嗣曹王臯為前軍兵馬使，鄂嶽團練使李兼副之，山南東道節度使賈耽為中軍兵馬使，荊南節度使張伯儀為後軍兵馬使，左神武軍使王價、左衛將軍高承謙、檢校太子詹事郭曙、檢校右庶子常願為押衙。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of War Xiao Fu was made chief administrator of the unified army; Hunan observation commissioner Kong Chaofu was left army chief of staff; Fan Ze, marching chief of staff of the Shannan East Circuit, was right chief of staff; Vice Director of Punishments Liu Congyi and censor Wei Xian were administrative aides; Vice Director of War Gao Can served as secretary; Right Golden Guard general Hun Jian was middle army provost marshal; Jiangxi governor and Acting Prince of Cao Li Gao was front army commander, with E-Yue training commissioner Li Jian as his deputy; Shannan East governor Jia Dan was middle army commander; Jingnan governor Zhang Boyi was rear army commander; Left Divine Martial Army commander Wang Jia, Left Guard general Gao Chengqian, acting crown prince steward Guo Shu, and acting right assistant to the heir apparent Chang Yuan served as yas.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Fu, Vice Minister of War, was made chief administrator of the unified army. Kong Chaofu, commissioner of Hunan, became left army chief of staff; Fan Ze, marching chief of staff of Shannan East, right chief of staff. Liu Congyi of the Ministry of Punishments and censor Wei Xian served as aides; Gao Can of the Ministry of War as secretary. Hun Jian, general of the Right Golden Guard, was provost marshal of the center. Li Gao, governor of Jiangxi and Acting Prince of Cao, commanded the vanguard, with Li Jian of E-Yue as his deputy; Jia Dan of Shannan East commanded the center; Zhang Boyi of Jingnan the rear. Wang Jia of the Left Divine Martial Army, Gao Chengqian of the Left Guard, Guo Shu as acting crown prince steward, and Chang Yuan as acting right assistant to the heir apparent served as yas.

sentences.zh: 未及行，涇原兵反，誼從帝出奉天。

translations.literal: Before he could depart, the Jingyuan garrison mutinied; Yi followed the emperor in flight to Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: Before the army could march, the Jingyuan garrison mutinied. Yi accompanied the emperor in flight to Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 硃泚攻城，誼晝夜傳勞諸軍不解帶。

translations.literal: When Zhu Ci besieged the city, Yi day and night relayed messages of encouragement to the armies without removing his belt.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci laid siege to the city, Yi went day and night among the troops bearing words of encouragement, never once loosening his belt.

sentences.zh: 帝還京師，復故封揚州大都督如故。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned to the capital, Yi's former title of governor-general of Yangzhou was restored as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to the capital, Yi's former appointment as governor-general of Yangzhou was restored unchanged.

sentences.zh: 永貞元年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Yongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 805.

sentences.zh: 通王諶，始王，拜開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Prince Tong Chen was first enfeoffed and appointed Grand Preceptor of the State, Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Tong Chen was first enfeoffed and granted the title of Grand Preceptor of the State, Third Rank.

sentences.zh: 貞元九年，領宣武節度大使，以李萬榮為留後，二年徙河東，以李說為留後，皆不出閤。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhenyuan he held the post of grand commissioner of Xuanwu, with Li Wanrong as acting commander; two years later he was transferred to Hedong, with Li Shuo as acting commander—all without leaving the palace confines.
translations.idiomatic: In 793 he was made grand commissioner of Xuanwu, with Li Wanrong as acting commander; two years later he was transferred to Hedong, with Li Shuo as acting commander—throughout without ever leaving the palace.

sentences.zh: 虔王諒，以王拜開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Prince Qian Liang, upon enfeoffment, was appointed Grand Preceptor of the State, Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Qian Liang, at the time of his enfeoffment, was granted the title of Grand Preceptor of the State, Third Rank.

sentences.zh: 貞元二年，領蔡州節度大使，以吳少誠為留後；

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyuan he was grand commissioner of Caizhou, with Wu Shaocheng as acting commander;
translations.idiomatic: In 786 he was made grand commissioner of Caizhou, with Wu Shaocheng as acting commander;

sentences.zh: 十年，徙節朔方靈鹽，以李欒為留後；

translations.literal: in the tenth year he was transferred to govern Shuofang-Lingyan, with Li Luan as acting commander;
translations.idiomatic: in 796 he was transferred to Shuofang-Lingyan, with Li Luan as acting commander;

sentences.zh: 明年，領橫海，又徙徐州，以程懷信、張愔為留後。

translations.literal: the following year he held Henghai, then was transferred again to Xuzhou, with Cheng Huaixin and Zhang Yin as acting commanders.
translations.idiomatic: the next year he took Henghai, then was moved again to Xuzhou, with Cheng Huaixin and Zhang Yin as acting commanders.

sentences.zh: 不出閤。

translations.literal: He did not leave the palace confines.
translations.idiomatic: He never left the palace.

sentences.zh: 肅王詳，資秀異，帝愛之。

translations.literal: Prince Su Xiang was gifted and exceptional in talent; the emperor loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Su Xiang was precocious and remarkable in talent, and the emperor loved him dearly.

sentences.zh: 建中二年薨，甫四歲。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Jianzhong, aged only four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 781 at the age of four.

sentences.zh: 帝欲用浮屠說，塔而不墳，禮儀判官李岧諫非禮，乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to follow a Buddhist monk's advice and bury him in a pagoda rather than a tomb; Ritual Administrator Li Tan remonstrated that this was improper, and the plan was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to heed a Buddhist monk and inter the boy in a pagoda instead of a tomb, but Li Tan, administrator of ritual, protested that this violated propriety, and the plan was set aside.

sentences.zh: 詔贈揚州大都督。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously made him governor-general of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously created him governor-general of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 文敬太子謜，見愛於帝，命為子。

translations.literal: Posthumous Crown Prince Wenjing Yuan was cherished by the emperor and ordered to be treated as his son.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan, posthumously styled Crown Prince Wenjing, was beloved of the emperor, who ordered that he be regarded as his own son.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，先諸王王邕。

translations.literal: In the early Zhenyuan era, before the other princes, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Zhenyuan era he was created Prince of Yong ahead of the other princes.

sentences.zh: 歷義武、昭義二軍節度大使，以張茂昭、王虔休為留後，不出閤。

translations.literal: He successively served as grand commissioner of the Yiwu and Zhaoyi armies, with Zhang Maozhao and Wang Qianxiu as acting commanders, without leaving the palace confines.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as grand commissioner of the Yiwu and Zhaoyi armies, with Zhang Maozhao and Wang Qianxiu as acting commanders, never leaving the palace.

sentences.zh: 十五年薨，年十八，追贈及謚。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he died, aged eighteen; posthumous honors and a temple name were granted.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 799 at the age of eighteen and was posthumously honored with title and temple name.

sentences.zh: 葬日，君臣以位而哭通化門外。

translations.literal: On the day of burial, ministers and officials wept according to rank outside Tonghua Gate.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of burial, ministers and officials took their places by rank and wept outside Tonghua Gate.

sentences.zh: 陵及廟置令、丞雲。

translations.literal: For his mausoleum and temple, directors and assistants were appointed, and so forth.
translations.idiomatic: Directors and assistants were appointed for his mausoleum and ancestral temple, and the like.

sentences.zh: 資王謙，亡薨年。

translations.literal: Prince Zi Qian: the year of death is unrecorded.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zi Qian: the year of his death is unrecorded.

sentences.zh: 代王諲，始王縉雲郡。

translations.literal: Prince Dai Yin was first Prince of Jinyun commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Dai Yin was first created Prince of Jinyun.

sentences.zh: 蚤薨，建中二年追王。

translations.literal: He died young; in the second year of Jianzhong he was posthumously enfeoffed as prince.
translations.idiomatic: He died in infancy; in 781 he was posthumously created a prince.

sentences.zh: 昭王誡，貞元二十一年始王。

translations.literal: Prince Zhao Jie was first enfeoffed in the twenty-first year of Zhenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhao Jie was first enfeoffed in 805.

sentences.zh: 亡薨年。

translations.literal: The year of death is unrecorded.
translations.idiomatic: The year of his death is unrecorded.

sentences.zh: 欽王諤，順宗即位，與珍王同封。

translations.literal: Prince Qin E: when Shunzong took the throne, he was enfeoffed together with the Prince of Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Qin E was enfeoffed when Shunzong ascended the throne, on the same occasion as the Prince of Zhen.

sentences.zh: 亡薨年。

translations.literal: The year of death is unrecorded.
translations.idiomatic: The year of his death is unrecorded.

sentences.zh: 珍王諴，大和六年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Zhen Yan died in the sixth year of Dahe.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhen Yan died in 832.

sentences.zh: 順宗二十七子：莊憲皇后生憲宗皇帝及綰，張昭訓生經，趙昭儀生結，王昭儀生總、約、緄；

translations.literal: Shunzong had twenty-seven sons: Empress Zhuangxian bore the future Emperor Xianzong and Wan; Zhang Zhaoxun bore Jing; Consort Zhao bore Jie; Consort Wang bore Zong, Yue, and Gun;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shunzong had twenty-seven sons. Empress Zhuangxian bore the future Emperor Xianzong and Wan; Zhang Zhaoxun bore Jing; Consort Zhao bore Jie; Consort Wang bore Zong, Yue, and Gun;

sentences.zh: 余二十王，史亡母之氏、位，四王蚤薨，亡官謚。

translations.literal: As for the remaining twenty princes, the histories do not record their mothers' clans or titles; four died young, with neither office nor posthumous title recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Of the remaining twenty princes, the histories have lost record of their mothers' clans and ranks; four died young, with neither office nor posthumous title preserved.

sentences.zh: 均王緯，初名沔。

translations.literal: Prince Jun Wei—originally named Mian.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jun Wei, originally named Mian.

sentences.zh: 王洋川，後進王。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Prince of Yangchuan, then advanced in rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was first created Prince of Yangchuan, then promoted in rank.

sentences.zh: 王三十三年，開成二年薨。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year of his princedom he died in the second year of Kaicheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year of his princedom he died, in 837.

sentences.zh: 漵王縱，初名洵。

translations.literal: Prince Xu Zong—originally named Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xu Zong, originally named Xun.

sentences.zh: 王臨淮，後進王。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Prince of Linhuai, then advanced in rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was first created Prince of Linhuai, then promoted in rank.

sentences.zh: 王三十二年，開成元年薨。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year of his princedom he died in the first year of Kaicheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year of his princedom he died, in 836.

sentences.zh: 莒王紓，初名浼。

translations.literal: Prince Ju Shu—originally named Mei.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ju Shu, originally named Mei.

sentences.zh: 為秘書監。

translations.literal: He served as director of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: He served as director of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 王弘農，後進王。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Prince of Hongnong, then advanced in rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was first created Prince of Hongnong, then promoted in rank.

sentences.zh: 王二十九年，大和八年薨。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of his princedom he died in the eighth year of Dahe.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year of his princedom he died, in 834.

sentences.zh: 密王綢，初名訁永。

translations.literal: Prince Mi Chou—originally named Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Mi Chou, originally named Yong.

sentences.zh: 王漢東，後進王。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Prince of Handong, then advanced in rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was first created Prince of Handong, then promoted in rank.

sentences.zh: 王三年，元和二年薨。

translations.literal: In the third year of his princedom he died in the second year of Yuanhe.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of his princedom he died, in 807.

sentences.zh: 邵王約，初名漵。

translations.literal: Prince Shao Yue—originally named Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shao Yue, originally named Xu.

sentences.zh: 為國子祭酒。

translations.literal: He served as director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He served as director of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 王高平，進王。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Prince of Gaoping, then advanced in rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was first created Prince of Gaoping, then promoted in rank.

sentences.zh: 王二年，元和元年薨。

translations.literal: In the second year of his princedom he died in the first year of Yuanhe.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of his princedom he died, in 806.

sentences.zh: 集王緗，初名淮。

translations.literal: Prince Ji Xiang—originally named Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ji Xiang, originally named Huai.

sentences.zh: 王宣城，進王。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Prince of Xuancheng, then advanced in rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was first created Prince of Xuancheng, then promoted in rank.

sentences.zh: 王十八年，長慶二年薨。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of his princedom he died in the second year of Changqing.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of his princedom he died, in 822.

sentences.zh: 冀王絿，初名湑。

translations.literal: Prince Ji Qiu—originally named Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ji Qiu, originally named Xu.

sentences.zh: 為太常卿。

translations.literal: He served as Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 王德陽，進王。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Prince of Deyang, then advanced in rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was first created Prince of Deyang, then promoted in rank.

sentences.zh: 王三十年，大和九年薨。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year of his princedom he died in the ninth year of Dahe.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year of his princedom he died, in 835.

sentences.zh: 和王綺，初名浥。

translations.literal: Prince He Qi—originally named Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Prince He Qi, originally named Yi.

sentences.zh: 王河東，進王。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Prince of Hedong, then advanced in rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was first created Prince of Hedong, then promoted in rank.

sentences.zh: 王二十八年，太和七年薨。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year of his princedom he died in the seventh year of Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year of his princedom he died, in 833.

sentences.zh: 衡王絢，王二十二年，寶歷二年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Heng Xuan: in the twenty-second year of his princedom he died in the second year of Baoli.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Heng Xuan died in the twenty-second year of his princedom, in 826.

sentences.zh: 會王纁，王六年，元和五年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Hui Xu: in the sixth year of his princedom he died in the fifth year of Yuanhe.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Hui Xu died in the sixth year of his princedom, in 810.

sentences.zh: 福王綰，歷魏博節度大使。

translations.literal: Prince Fu Wan had served as military commissioner of Wei and Bo.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Fu Wan had served as military commissioner of Wei and Bo.

sentences.zh: 咸通元年，進拜司空。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiantong he was promoted to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In 860 he was promoted to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 王五十七年，咸通二年薨。

translations.literal: In the fifty-seventh year of his princedom he died in the second year of Xiantong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-seventh year of his princedom he died, in 861.

sentences.zh: 珍王繕，初名況。

translations.literal: Prince Zhen Shan—originally named Kuang.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhen Shan, originally named Kuang.

sentences.zh: 王洛交，後進王。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Prince of Luojiao, then advanced in rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was first created Prince of Luojiao, then promoted in rank.

sentences.zh: 亡薨年。

translations.literal: The year of death is unrecorded.
translations.idiomatic: The year of his death is unrecorded.

sentences.zh: 撫王纮，咸通初，歷司空，又進司徒、太尉。

translations.literal: Prince Fu Hong: at the beginning of the Xiantong era he served in succession as Minister of Works, then was promoted to Grand Minister and Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Fu Hong: in the early Xiantong era he served successively as Minister of Works, then was promoted to Grand Minister and Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 王七十三年，乾符三年薨。

translations.literal: In the seventy-third year of his princedom he died in the third year of Qianfu.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventy-third year of his princedom he died, in 876.

sentences.zh: 嶽王緄，王二十三年，太和二年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Yue Gun: in the twenty-third year of his princedom he died in the second year of Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yue Gun died in the twenty-third year of his princedom, in 827.

sentences.zh: 袁王紳，王五十六年，咸通元年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Yuan Shen: in the fifty-sixth year of his princedom he died in the first year of Xiantong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yuan Shen died in the fifty-sixth year of his princedom, in 860.

sentences.zh: 桂王綸，王十年，元和九年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Gui Lun: in the tenth year of his princedom he died in the ninth year of Yuanhe.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Gui Lun died in the tenth year of his princedom, in 814.

sentences.zh: 翼王綽，王五十八年，咸通三年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Yi Chuo: in the fifty-eighth year of his princedom he died in the third year of Xiantong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yi Chuo died in the fifty-eighth year of his princedom, in 862.

sentences.zh: 蘄王緝，王六年，咸通八年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Qi Ji: in the sixth year of his princedom he died in the eighth year of Xiantong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Qi Ji died in the sixth year of his princedom, in 867.

sentences.zh: 欽王績，亡薨年。

translations.literal: Prince Qin Ji: the year of death is unrecorded.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Qin Ji: the year of his death is unrecorded.

sentences.zh: 憲宗二十子：紀美人生寧，懿安皇后生穆宗皇帝，孝明皇后生宣宗皇帝；

translations.literal: Xianzong had twenty sons: Consort Ji Mei bore Ning; Empress Yian bore Emperor Muzong; Empress Xiaoming bore Emperor Xuanzong;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong had twenty sons. Consort Ji Mei bore Ning; Empress Yian bore Emperor Muzong; Empress Xiaoming bore Emperor Xuanzong;

sentences.zh: 余十七王，皆後宮所生，史逸其母之號、氏。

translations.literal: As for the remaining seventeen princes, all were born to women of the inner palace; the histories have lost record of their mothers' titles and clans.
translations.idiomatic: Of the remaining seventeen princes, all were born to women of the inner palace; the histories have lost record of their mothers' titles and clans.

sentences.zh: 惠昭太子寧，貞元二十一年，始王平原，與同安、彭城、高密、文安四王同封。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Huizhao Ning: in the twenty-first year of Zhenyuan he was first enfeoffed as Prince of Pingyuan, together with the four princes of Tong'an, Pengcheng, Gaomi, and Wen'an.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Huizhao Ning was first created Prince of Pingyuan in 805, enfeoffed on the same occasion as the Princes of Tong'an, Pengcheng, Gaomi, and Wen'an.

sentences.zh: 帝即位，進王鄧，與澧、深、洋、絳四王同封。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne, he was advanced to Prince of Deng, enfeoffed together with the four princes of Li, Shen, Yang, and Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzong ascended the throne, Ning was promoted to Prince of Deng and enfeoffed together with the Princes of Li, Shen, Yang, and Jiang.

sentences.zh: 於是國嗣未立，李絳等建言：「聖人以天下為大器，知一人不可獨化，四海不可無本，故建太子以自副，然後人心定，宗祏安，有國不易之常道。

translations.literal: At that time the heir had not yet been established. Li Jiang and others submitted a memorial: 'The sage treats all under Heaven as a great vessel, knowing that one man cannot transform it alone and that the four seas cannot be without a foundation. Therefore he establishes a crown prince as his deputy—only then are hearts settled, the ancestral temple secure, and the unchanging way of holding a state preserved.
translations.idiomatic: The heir had not yet been named. Li Jiang and others memorialized the throne: 'The sage treats the empire as a great vessel. He knows that no single man can transform it alone, and that the realm cannot stand without a root. He therefore establishes a crown prince as his deputy—only then are hearts settled, the ancestral temple secure, and the unchanging way of holding a state preserved.

sentences.zh: 陛下受命四年，而冢子未建，是開窺覦之端，乖慎重之義，非所以承列聖，示萬世。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has received the Mandate for four years, yet the heir has not been established. This opens the door to covetous eyes and departs from the principle of prudent caution. It is not the way to inherit the line of sage emperors and show the path to ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has reigned four years, yet no heir has been named. This invites scheming ambition and departs from the duty of prudent caution. It is not the way to inherit the line of sage emperors and show the path to ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「善。

translations.literal: ' The emperor said: 'Well said.
translations.idiomatic: ' The emperor said, 'Well said.

sentences.zh: 」以寧為皇太子，更名宙，前以制示絳等。

translations.literal: ' He made Ning crown prince, changed his name to Zhou, and beforehand showed the edict to Jiang and the others.
translations.idiomatic: ' He made Ning crown prince, changed his name to Zhou, and beforehand showed the edict to Jiang and the others.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復初名。

translations.literal: Before long he reverted to his original name.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he reverted to his original name.

sentences.zh: 冊禮用孟夏，雨，不克，改用孟秋，亦雨，冬十月克行禮。

translations.literal: The investiture was scheduled for early summer, but rain prevented it; it was rescheduled for early autumn, but rain fell again; in the tenth month of winter the ceremony was finally completed.
translations.idiomatic: The investiture was set for early summer, but rain forced a postponement; rescheduled for early autumn, rain fell again; only in the tenth month of winter was the ceremony finally held.

sentences.zh: 明年薨，年十九。

translations.literal: The next year he died, aged nineteen.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he died, aged nineteen.

sentences.zh: 澧王惲，始王同安，後進王。

translations.literal: Prince Li Yun was first enfeoffed as Prince of Tong'an, then advanced in rank.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Li Yun was first created Prince of Tong'an, then promoted in rank.

sentences.zh: 惠昭之喪，吐突承璀議復立儲副，意屬惲，帝自以穆宗為太子。

translations.literal: At Crown Prince Huizhao's funeral, Tu Tu Chengcui proposed reestablishing an heir and favored Yun; the emperor himself made Muzong crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: At Crown Prince Huizhao's funeral, Tu Tu Chengcui urged that a new heir be named and favored Yun—but the emperor himself installed Muzong as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 帝崩之夕，承璀死，王被殺，秘不發喪，久之以告，廢朝三日。

translations.literal: On the night the emperor died, Chengcui was killed and the prince was executed; the death was kept secret and mourning was not announced until long afterward, then court mourning was suspended for three days.
translations.idiomatic: On the night the emperor died, Chengcui was put to death and the prince was killed. The death was kept secret; mourning was not announced until long afterward, and court was suspended for three days.

sentences.zh: 三子：曰漢，王東陽郡；

translations.literal: Three sons: Han was enfeoffed Prince of Dongyang commandery;
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Han was created Prince of Dongyang commandery;

sentences.zh: 曰源，安陸；

translations.literal: Yuan at Anlu;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan at Anlu;

sentences.zh: 曰演，臨安。

translations.literal: Yan at Lin'an.
translations.idiomatic: and Yan at Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 初，惲名寬，深王察，洋王寰，絳王寮，建王審，元和七年，並改今名。

translations.literal: Initially Yun was named Kuan; the Prince of Shen was named Cha; the Prince of Yang was named Huan; the Prince of Jiang was named Liao; the Prince of Jian was named Shen; in the seventh year of Yuanhe all received their present names.
translations.idiomatic: At first Yun was named Kuan; the Prince of Shen was named Cha; the Prince of Yang, Huan; the Prince of Jiang, Liao; the Prince of Jian, Shen—in 812 all received their present names.

sentences.zh: 深王悰，始王彭城郡，進王深。

translations.literal: Prince Shen Cong was first enfeoffed as Prince of Pengcheng commandery, then advanced to Prince of Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shen Cong was first created Prince of Pengcheng commandery, then promoted to Prince of Shen.

sentences.zh: 子潭王河內，淑吳興。

translations.literal: His sons: Tan was Prince of Henei; Shu was Prince of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Tan, Prince of Henei, and Shu, Prince of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 洋王忻，始王高密，進王洋。

translations.literal: Prince Yang Xin was first enfeoffed as Prince of Gaomi, then advanced to Prince of Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yang Xin was first created Prince of Gaomi, then promoted to Prince of Yang.

sentences.zh: 大和二年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Dahe.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 828.

sentences.zh: 子沛王潁川郡。

translations.literal: His son Pei was Prince of Yingchuan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Pei was created Prince of Yingchuan commandery.

sentences.zh: 絳王悟，始王文安，進王。

translations.literal: Prince Jiang Wu was first enfeoffed as Prince of Wen'an, then advanced in rank.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jiang Wu was first created Prince of Wen'an, then promoted in rank.

sentences.zh: 敬宗崩，蘇佐明等矯詔以王領軍國事。

translations.literal: When Jingzong died, Su Zuoming and others forged an edict making the prince regent of state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingzong died, Su Zuoming and others forged an edict placing the prince in charge of state affairs.

sentences.zh: 王守澄等立文宗，王見殺。

translations.literal: Wang Shoucheng and others enthroned Wenzong, and the prince was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shoucheng and his faction enthroned Wenzong, and the prince was put to death.

sentences.zh: 二子：洙王新安，滂高平。

translations.literal: Two sons: Zhu was Prince of Xin'an; Pang was Prince of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Zhu, Prince of Xin'an, and Pang, Prince of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 建王恪，元和元年始封。

translations.literal: Prince Jian Ke was first enfeoffed in the first year of Yuanhe.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jian Ke was first enfeoffed in 806.

sentences.zh: 時淄青節度使李師古死，其弟師道丐符節，故詔恪為鄆州大都督、平盧軍淄青等州節度大使，以師道為留後，然不出閤。

translations.literal: At that time the military commissioner of Zi-Qing, Li Shigu, had died; his brother Shidao begged for the commission. An edict therefore made Ke Grand Protector of Yan prefecture and military commissioner of Pinglu, Zi, and Qing, with Shidao as acting commissioner—but Ke did not leave the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Shigu, military commissioner of Zi-Qing, died, his brother Shidao petitioned for the commission. The court therefore made Ke Grand Protector of Yan and military commissioner of Pinglu, Zi, and Qing, with Shidao as acting commissioner—but Ke never left the palace.

sentences.zh: 長慶元年薨，無嗣。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Changqing, leaving no heir.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 821, leaving no heir.

sentences.zh: 鄜王憬，長慶元年始王，與瓊、沔、婺、茂、淄、衢、澶七王同封。

translations.literal: Prince Fen Jing was first enfeoffed in the first year of Changqing, together with the seven princes of Qiong, Mian, Wu, Mao, Zi, Qu, and Chan.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Fen Jing was first enfeoffed in 821, together with the Princes of Qiong, Mian, Wu, Mao, Zi, Qu, and Chan.

sentences.zh: 開成四年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the fourth year of Kaicheng.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 839.

sentences.zh: 子溥平陽郡王。

translations.literal: His son Pu was Prince of Pingyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Pu was created Prince of Pingyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 瓊王悅，子津河間郡王。

translations.literal: Prince Qiong Yue: his son Jin was Prince of Hejian commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Qiong Yue's son Jin was created Prince of Hejian commandery.

sentences.zh: 沔王恂，子瀛晉陵郡王。

translations.literal: Prince Mian Xiong: his son Ying was Prince of Jinling commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Mian Xiong's son Ying was created Prince of Jinling commandery.

sentences.zh: 婺王懌，子清新平郡王。

translations.literal: Prince Wu Yi: his son Qing was Prince of Xinping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wu Yi's son Qing was created Prince of Xinping commandery.

sentences.zh: 茂王愔，子潓武功郡王。

translations.literal: Prince Mao Yin: his son Sui was Prince of Wugong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Mao Yin's son Sui was created Prince of Wugong commandery.

sentences.zh: 淄王忄辦，開成元年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Zi Xie died in the first year of Kaicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zi Xie died in 836.

sentences.zh: 子浣許昌郡王，渙馮翊郡王。

translations.literal: His sons: Wan was Prince of Xuchang commandery; Huan was Prince of Fengyi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Wan, Prince of Xuchang commandery, and Huan, Prince of Fengyi commandery.

sentences.zh: 衢王詹，子涉晉平郡王。

translations.literal: Prince Qu Zhan: his son She was Prince of Jinping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Qu Zhan's son She was created Prince of Jinping commandery.

sentences.zh: 澶王忄充，子濘雁門郡王。

translations.literal: Prince Chan Chen: his son Ning was Prince of Yanmen commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Chan Chen's son Ning was created Prince of Yanmen commandery.

sentences.zh: 棣王惴，大中六年始王，與彭、信二王同封。

translations.literal: Prince Di Zhuai was first enfeoffed in the sixth year of Dazhong, together with the two princes of Peng and Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Di Zhuai was first enfeoffed in 852, together with the Princes of Peng and Xin.

sentences.zh: 咸通三年薨，無嗣。

translations.literal: He died in the third year of Xiantong, leaving no heir.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 862, leaving no heir.

sentences.zh: 彭王惕，乾寧中，韓建殺之石堤谷。

translations.literal: Prince Peng Ti: in the Qianning era Han Jian killed him at Shidi Valley.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Peng Ti: during the Qianning era Han Jian killed him at Shidi Valley.

sentences.zh: 無嗣。

translations.literal: He left no heir.
translations.idiomatic: He left no heir.

sentences.zh: 信王憻，咸通八年薨，無嗣。

translations.literal: Prince Xin Tan died in the eighth year of Xiantong, leaving no heir.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xin Tan died in 867, leaving no heir.

sentences.zh: 榮王忄責，咸通三年始王。

translations.literal: Prince Rong Zhi was first enfeoffed in the third year of Xiantong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Rong Zhi was first enfeoffed in 862.

sentences.zh: 廣明初，拜司空。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Guangming era he was appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Guangming era (c. 880) he was appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 子令平嗣王。

translations.literal: His son Ling succeeded to the princedom.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ling succeeded to the princedom.

sentences.zh: 凡八王，史失其薨年。

translations.literal: In all, eight princes—the histories have lost the year of their deaths.
translations.idiomatic: Eight princes in all—the histories have lost record of the year of their deaths.

sentences.zh: 穆宗五子：恭僖皇后生敬宗皇帝，貞獻皇后生文宗皇帝，宣懿皇后生武宗皇帝；

translations.literal: Muzong had five sons: Empress Gongxi bore Emperor Jingzong; Empress Zhenxian bore Emperor Wenzong; Empress Xuanyi bore Emperor Wuzong;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Muzong had five sons. Empress Gongxi bore Emperor Jingzong; Empress Zhenxian bore Emperor Wenzong; Empress Xuanyi bore Emperor Wuzong;

sentences.zh: 余二王，亡其母之氏、位。

translations.literal: As for the remaining two princes, the histories have lost record of their mothers' clans and ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Of the remaining two princes, the histories have lost record of their mothers' clans and ranks.

sentences.zh: 安王溶。

translations.literal: Prince An Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince An Rong.

sentences.zh: 初，楊賢妃得寵於文宗，晚稍多疾，妃陰請以王為嗣，密為自安地。

translations.literal: At first Consort Yang Xian enjoyed Wenzong's favor; in her later years she fell often ill. The consort secretly asked that the prince be made heir, quietly securing a refuge for herself.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Yang Xian had long enjoyed Wenzong's favor; as she grew ill in her later years, she secretly petitioned that Prince An be named heir—quietly securing a refuge for herself.

sentences.zh: 帝與宰相李玨謀，玨謂不可，乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor consulted Chancellor Li Jue; Jue said it could not be done, and the plan was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor consulted Chancellor Li Jue, who declared it impossible, and the plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 乃帝崩，仇士良立武宗，欲重己功，即擿溶嘗欲以為太子事，殺之。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, Qiu Shiliang enthroned Wuzong and, wishing to magnify his own achievement, immediately exposed Rong's past attempt to be made crown prince and had him killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzong died, Qiu Shiliang enthroned Wuzong and, wishing to magnify his own achievement, immediately exposed Rong's past attempt to be made crown prince and had him put to death.

sentences.zh: 敬宗五子：妃郭氏生普，余四王，亡母之氏、位。

translations.literal: Jingzong had five sons: Consort Guo bore Pu; as for the remaining four princes, the histories have lost record of their mothers' clans and ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jingzong had five sons. Consort Guo bore Pu; of the remaining four princes, the histories have lost record of their mothers' clans and ranks.

sentences.zh: 文宗二子：王德妃生永，後宮生宗儉。

translations.literal: Wenzong had two sons: Consort Wang De bore Yong; a woman of the inner palace bore Zongjian.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong had two sons. Consort Wang De bore Yong; a woman of the inner palace bore Zongjian.

sentences.zh: 莊恪太子永，大和四年始王魯。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Zhuangke Yong was first enfeoffed as Prince of Lu in the fourth year of Dahe.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Zhuangke Yong was first created Prince of Lu in 830.

sentences.zh: 帝以王幼，宜得賢輔，因召見傅和元亮。

translations.literal: The emperor thought the prince was young and ought to have worthy tutors, and therefore summoned the tutor He Yuanliang for an audience.
translations.idiomatic: Thinking the prince too young to govern without guidance, the emperor summoned his tutor He Yuanliang for an audience.

sentences.zh: 元亮以卒史進，有所問，不能答。

translations.literal: Yuanliang had risen from the rank of clerk; when questioned he could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanliang had risen from the rank of clerk; when the emperor questioned him, he could not answer.

sentences.zh: 帝責謂宰相：「王可教，官屬應任士大夫賢者，寧元亮比邪！

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked the chancellors: 'The prince can be taught; his staff ought to be worthy gentlemen of the scholar-official class—is Yuanliang fit for such company?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked the chancellors: 'The prince can be taught. His staff ought to be worthy gentlemen of the scholar-official class—is Yuanliang fit for such company?

sentences.zh: 」於是劇選戶部侍郎庾敬休兼王傅，太常卿鄭肅兼長史，戶部郎中李踐方兼司馬。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon Vice Minister of Revenue Yu Jingxiu was rigorously selected as the prince's tutor; Minister of Ceremonies Zheng Su was made chief administrator; and Director of Revenue Li Jianfang was made chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: ' Thereupon Yu Jingxiu, Vice Minister of Revenue, was rigorously chosen as the prince's tutor; Zheng Su, Minister of Ceremonies, as chief administrator; and Li Jianfang, Director of Revenue, as chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 六年，遂立為皇太子。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was thereupon established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was thereupon established as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 帝承寶歷荒怠，身勤儉率天下，謂晉王生謹敏，欲引為嗣，會蚤夭，故久不議東宮事。

translations.literal: The emperor, succeeding the reckless neglect of the Baoli era, personally modeled thrift and led the empire by example. He regarded the Prince of Jin as by nature prudent and quick-witted and wished to install him as heir—but the prince died prematurely, and therefore he long deferred discussion of the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Succeeding the reckless neglect of the Baoli era, the emperor personally modeled thrift and led the empire by example. He had regarded the Prince of Jin as prudent and quick-witted from youth and wished to make him heir—but the prince died prematurely, and therefore he long deferred naming a crown prince.

sentences.zh: 及太子立，天下屬心焉。

translations.literal: When the crown prince was established, all under Heaven looked to him with hope.
translations.idiomatic: Once the crown prince was established, all under Heaven looked to him with hope.

sentences.zh: 開成三年，詔宮臣詣崇明門謁朔望，侍讀偶日入對。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaicheng, an edict ordered palace officials to attend at Chongming Gate on the new and full moon; tutors occasionally entered for audience by day.
translations.idiomatic: In 838 an edict ordered palace officials to attend at Chongming Gate on the new and full moon; tutors occasionally entered for audience by day.

sentences.zh: 太子稍事燕豫，不能壹循法，保傅戒告， 不納。

translations.literal: The crown prince gradually gave himself to banquets and pleasures and could not wholly follow the rules; his tutors admonished him, but he would not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince gradually gave himself to banquets and pleasures and could not wholly follow the rules; his tutors admonished him, but he would not listen.

sentences.zh: 又母愛弛，楊賢妃方幸，數譖之。

translations.literal: Moreover his mother's love grew slack; Consort Yang Xian was then in favor and slandered him repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover his mother's affection waned; Consort Yang Xian, then in favor, slandered him again and again.

sentences.zh: 帝它日震怒，禦延英，引見群臣，詔曰：「太子多過失，不可屬天下，其議廢之。

translations.literal: One day the emperor, shaken with rage, held court at Yanying Hall, summoned the ministers, and proclaimed: "The crown prince has many faults and cannot be entrusted with all under Heaven—discuss deposing him.
translations.idiomatic: One day the emperor, shaken with rage, held court at Yanying Hall, summoned the ministers, and proclaimed: "The crown prince has many faults and cannot be entrusted with the realm—discuss deposing him.

sentences.zh: 」群臣頓首言：「太子春秋盛，雖有過，尚可改。

translations.literal: " The ministers prostrated themselves and said: "The crown prince is in the prime of youth; though he has faults, he can still reform.
translations.idiomatic: " The ministers prostrated themselves and said: "The crown prince is still young; though he has faults, he can still reform.

sentences.zh: 且天下本，不可輕動，惟陛下幸赦。

translations.literal: Moreover he is the foundation of the realm and must not be lightly moved—we beg Your Majesty's mercy.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover he is the foundation of the realm and must not be lightly displaced—we beg Your Majesty's mercy.

sentences.zh: 」御史中丞狄兼暮流涕固爭，帝未決，罷。

translations.literal: " Vice Censor-in-Chief Di Jianmo wept and argued firmly; the emperor remained undecided and dismissed court.

translations.literal: The commentator says: From the mid-Tang onward, imperial clansmen mostly dwelt in the capital; the younger ones often never left the palace confines. Though titled as kings of states, in truth they differed little from common men of the lanes. Thus they performed no grand evil, yet neither could they lend weight to the royal house; when fortune reached its limit there was no return—they perished together with Tang.
